title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Shared radix-4 combinational DIV/REM datapath
motivation:
The baseline scores 12.12 at a median 5.442 MHz. Its reported worst
path is 199.837 ns across 156 cells, passing through forwarding and
u_ex/u_alu. The ALU implements signed and unsigned division and remainder
with separate / and % expressions, making long combinational division
the strongest candidate for this unusually deep arithmetic path. Even
infrequent DIV/REM instructions constrain the clock for all CoreMark
instructions. No prior optimization attempts are recorded in log.jsonl,
and LESSONS.md is absent.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU arithmetic inside alu.sv with one
shared, fully combinational unsigned radix-4 restoring divmod network,
surrounded by RV32M signed-magnitude conversion and result correction.
This is a local arithmetic implementation change: keep the ALU ports,
zero-cycle combinational latency, pipeline, forwarding, bus stalls,
retirement width, and all non-division operations unchanged.

Consume the dividend from most significant to least significant in
sixteen two-bit digits. Precompute unsigned D, 2D, and 3D at 34 bits
without truncating their high bits. At each stage form T = (R << 2)
| next_digit, and compute T-D, T-2D, and T-3D in parallel. Select the
largest digit whose subtraction has no borrow, or digit zero with
remainder T. Use subtraction carry/borrow to select the digit rather
than a separate magnitude comparison followed by subtraction. Emit
both the quotient digits and the final remainder from this one network;
do not implement remainder with a second divider or a quotient multiply.

Make the sixteen stages explicit with compile-time bounds so synthesis
sees their widths. After consuming k digits, the remainder is bounded
by the consumed 2k-bit dividend prefix. Stage k therefore needs a
2k-bit trial value and a 2k+1-bit unsigned subtraction. A candidate
multiple of D is eligible only if all its bits above that 2k-bit width
are zero AND its subtraction has no borrow. This high-bit guard is
required for correctness when the divisor is larger than the prefix;
truncating the divisor without the guard is incorrect. Keep only the
selected low 2k remainder bits for the next stage. This produces
sixteen dependent digit-selection stages with increasing arithmetic
width instead of a conventional thirty-two-step binary division chain.

For DIV and REM, convert negative operands to unsigned 32-bit magnitudes,
including magnitude 0x80000000 for INT_MIN. Negate the quotient iff the
operand signs differ; negate the remainder iff the dividend is negative.
DIVU and REMU use the original unsigned operands. Explicitly override
divisor zero with quotient 0xffffffff and remainder equal to the original
dividend, before sign correction can corrupt those results. Preserve
INT_MIN/-1 as quotient 0x80000000 and remainder zero. Preserve all eight
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas exactly, and exclude the real divider from
that build. Leave multiplier expressions and other ALU operations alone.

The predicted gain comes from a shorter divider dependency chain and
sharing quotient/remainder hardware, with no instruction-cycle penalty.
The main uncertainty is Gowin mapping: three parallel trial subtractors
and digit selection may offset the reduction in dependent stages.
Confirm the change with real-arithmetic ALU tests, the existing formal
and cosimulation gates, canonical CoreMark UART/CRC checks, and median
Gowin timing under the unchanged bus-stall model. Fitness must exceed
12.67752 to clear the champion's 4.6 percent acceptance margin; the
following impact is a prediction, not a measured result.

title: Move division off the single-cycle EX path with a shared clocked divider
motivation:
The sole recorded baseline scores 12.12 iterations/s at 5.442 MHz. Its
worst reported path is 199.837 ns through forwarding and the EX ALU,
with 156 cells. The ALU currently evaluates full-width signed and
unsigned division and remainder combinationally. This strongly suggests
that the unrolled divider constrains the clock for every instruction,
although a detailed cell-level timing report must confirm the inference.
There is no LESSONS.md and no previous structural attempt in log.jsonl.
Breaking this arithmetic dependency across clock edges is a substantially
larger opportunity than the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the combinational DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU execution path with one
shared, blocking, clocked divider. Keep the existing single-cycle base
ALU and multiplier paths. Capture the forwarded operands and operation
once, normalize signed operands to unsigned magnitudes, and reuse an
eight-step radix-2 restoring divide datapath for four iteration clocks.
Each step shifts the partial remainder and quotient/dividend and uses
one 33-bit trial subtraction to select the next remainder and quotient
bit. Register normalization before iteration and register sign correction
after iteration, so neither forwarding nor result negation is chained
through all 32 quotient steps. Quotient and remainder come from the same
state; select the requested result after signed correction. Use explicit
RV32M handling for division by zero and INT_MIN/-1. Do not introduce a
second combinational division path or implement the iteration with / or %.

Add a request/completion handshake at EX. A divide starts only for a
valid instruction when the older MEM operation can advance. Hold PC and
ID/EX until the result transfers, but let older MEM/WB instructions drain.
On divide-wait cycles clear the entire outgoing EX/MEM bundle once any
older memory transaction is accepted; merely clearing valid is unsafe
because existing memory and forwarding enables also use control fields.
A data-memory stall retains priority and preserves its pending request.
Capture the forwarded source values at launch for both arithmetic and
RVFI, since older forwarding sources disappear while the divide runs.
Keep completion and result stable until EX/MEM accepts them, consume each
request exactly once, and release the held younger instruction on that
transfer. Its dependency on the divide then uses ordinary EX/MEM or
MEM/WB forwarding. Prevent repeated launch, repeated stores, duplicate
retirement, and redirects from invalid or unaccepted EX instructions.

Use the same launch, busy, completion, and retirement schedule under
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS; only the arithmetic result changes to the existing
per-operation XOR stand-in computed from captured operands. A normal
operation should take six internal clocks (capture/normalization, four
iteration clocks, and result correction), then transfer on the next
available EX/MEM edge. Check that this bounded latency passes the
unmodified 20-step instruction and liveness checks, including consecutive
divides. Preserve the nret=1 top-level interface and every invariant.

This single structural change trades a few cycles per division for a
shorter global critical path and less duplicated arithmetic. Division
frequency in the bracketed CoreMark region is not yet measured, so
validate the product of iterations/cycle and median Gowin Fmax, not Fmax
alone. Require fitness above 12.67752 iterations/s with canonical CRCs,
marker timing, and the existing random stalls. Run the unchanged formal,
cosim, and unit-test gates; inspect the new Gowin worst path to verify
that the original full-width divider chain has actually disappeared.

title: Compact bimodal branch prediction with immediate direct targets
motivation:
The baseline fetches sequentially and redirects every taken branch and jump
from EX. Although described as five stages, IF/ID is combinational, so each
such redirect discards one younger fetch slot. Repeated loops and direct
jumps in CoreMark therefore incur avoidable bubbles on top of the roughly
22 percent bus stalls. The sole recorded experiment is the baseline; there
are no prior predictor attempts or LESSONS.md. Its reported critical path
crosses forwarding and the combinational ALU, so a small predictor can
improve iterations per cycle without attempting to change that arithmetic
path. Any frequency benefit is excluded from the expected gain.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact next-PC prediction mechanism to the existing combinational
fetch/decode stage: a 64-entry table of two-bit saturating direction counters
indexed by fetch PC[7:2], reset to weakly taken (2'b10). For a legal BRANCH
encoding, use the counter MSB and compute its target directly from the
current instruction's sign-extended B immediate. Predict legal JAL taken
using its J immediate. Permit taken predictions only for word-aligned
direct targets. All other instructions, including JALR, predict PC+4.
This uses no target table, tags, return stack, or speculative history.

Advance the PC to the predicted next address only when the instruction is
accepted into ID/EX. Carry a single predicted_taken bit alongside that
instruction, resetting it on bubbles and holding it with the entire ID/EX
payload during stalls. A full predicted-target register is unnecessary:
every predicted target is a direct PC-relative target recomputed exactly
in EX from the same instruction. Keep io_imemAddr driven by the PC register;
prediction must not create a combinational instruction-memory address loop.

Resolve conditions and targets with the existing forwarded EX operands.
For direct branches and JAL, redirect only when predicted_taken differs
from the actual legal, aligned transfer decision. A failed taken prediction
redirects to the branch's PC+4; a missed taken prediction uses its resolved
target. Unpredicted legal aligned JALR retains EX redirection and bit-zero
masking. Invalid instructions never redirect or train. Illegal encodings
and misaligned targets retain existing trap, write suppression, and linear
PC behavior. RVFI pc_next always records the architectural resolved next PC,
independently of prediction. Correct predictions must not flush fetch/ID.

Apply recovery and train the counter exactly once when a valid instruction
advances from EX into EX/MEM. Train only legal conditional branches without
a target-alignment fault, saturating toward their resolved taken/not-taken
outcome and indexing with the resolving instruction's PC[7:2]. Read the
current counter for the update, so aliasing or intervening updates cannot
be overwritten by a stale counter snapshot. Define simultaneous lookup and
training as lookup of the pre-edge state; either prediction remains safe
because EX verifies it. Do not train JAL, JALR, bubbles, or held branches.

During a dmem stall, hold PC, prediction metadata, and ID/EX, and defer
recovery until EX can advance. On that advance, misprediction recovery
overrides imem not-ready and load-use holds and squashes the younger fetch
slot. Under imem stalls or load-use bubbles, do not consume a new prediction.
Preserve the existing MEM/WB forwarding retention during dmem stalls.
These rules prevent duplicate training, lost corrections, and wrong-path
stores while retaining the single-channel nret=1 retirement contract.

The testable expectation is approximately 8-12 percent fewer measured
CoreMark cycles, with a small possible routing/frequency cost, yielding
about 8 percent net fitness improvement over 12.12. This is an estimate,
not a measured branch profile. The acceptance boundary is above 12.67752;
at unchanged Fmax this requires over 4.40 percent fewer bracketed cycles.
Validate architectural behavior with directed prediction/stall tests,
existing cocotb and formal gates, and stalled cosimulation; then use the
unchanged CoreMark markers, canonical CRC checks, and median Gowin Fmax
to establish whether the net gain exceeds 4.6 percent. Table aliasing,
overlap with existing stalls, and placement effects are the main risks.

title: Shorten the divider feedback path with six restoring steps per clock
motivation:
The champion scores 70.52 at 31.675 MHz. Its reported worst path starts
and ends at u_divider/remainder_q, with a 36.847 ns arrival and 252 cells;
eight dependent restoring subtract/select steps remain in each clock.
LESSONS.md records that clocking the divider produced the major gain.
The prior micro_opt attempt at a fully combinational radix-4 divider
reached only 5.749 MHz, so preserving the clocked design is essential.
Baseline and champion both report 4,491,485 bracketed CoreMark cycles,
suggesting that longer division latency has negligible measured cost
in this workload. A local reduction in divider unrolling directly
targets the measured critical path without changing the CPU pipeline.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change only the existing blocking divider's unroll factor from eight
to six radix-2 restoring steps per iteration clock. Execute five full
six-step iterations followed by one two-step iteration, processing
exactly 32 dividend bits. Preserve the current capture/normalization,
correction, and held-completion states and every request/result port.
This is an arithmetic micro-optimization within the existing unit,
not a new execution architecture or a new division algorithm.

Keep quotient_step and remainder_step entries 0 through 6, and six
33-bit shifted/trial subtraction pairs. Preserve the existing full
subtraction width and borrow-based remainder/quotient selection.
Widen iteration_q to three bits. At iteration values 0 through 4,
register step[6]; at iteration 5, register step[2] and enter CORRECT.
Do not execute six effective shifts in the last iteration, which
would incorrectly divide a 36-bit shifted dividend. The final-step
choice depends only on the registered counter, not arithmetic data.
Retain registered sign correction, division-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1
handling, signed quotient truncation, and dividend-signed remainder.

The revised fixed schedule is eight internal rising edges including
capture: capture at edge 1, six iteration edges 2 through 7, and
correction/result_valid at edge 8; the earliest result transfer is
edge 9. Keep this identical under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, preserving all
four existing division/remainder substitution constants and captured
operands. Preserve reset cancellation, stable DONE results under
backpressure, and exactly one launch and transfer per instruction.
Existing EX and hazard handshakes should require no functional edits.

Six steps deliberately limit the latency increase to two clocks.
Four steps would require eight iterations and an eleven-cycle
consecutive-divide retirement interval, risking the unchanged formal
liveness window from trigger 10 to check 20. With six steps the
ordinary consecutive-divide interval is nine clocks, leaving one
clock for a preceding load-use bubble or taken redirect. Validate
those boundary sequences using the existing formal configuration;
never relax its depths, liveness assertion, or any other invariant.

Cutting the dominant feedback chain by 25 percent should improve
median Gowin Fmax enough to exceed the 4.6 percent acceptance margin,
while the logged CoreMark cycle counts suggest little IPC penalty.
A 20 percent fitness improvement is a prediction, not a measurement;
counter-selection overhead, routing, and a newly dominant multiplier
or forwarding path may limit it. Run real and ALTOPS ALU tests, pipeline
tests, unchanged formal and cosimulation gates, canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART and marker checks, and median Gowin timing. Require measured
fitness above 73.76392, using the actual new bracketed cycle count.
Preserve nret=1, decoder behavior, memory handshakes, and all external
ports. Do not optimize RVFI-only logic or change evaluation files.

worst path runs from remainder_q back to remainder_q inside u_divider,

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition the existing shared blocking radix-2 divider from four
iterations of eight restoring steps into six iteration clocks with a
maximum of six steps per clock. Perform six steps on iterations 0..4
and exactly two steps on iteration 5, consuming 32 dividend bits in
total. Keep operand capture and signed normalization on the request
edge, and keep result selection and sign correction in a separate
registered CORRECT state. This is one structural change to the amount
of arithmetic performed between divider state registers.

Retain one reused six-step subtract/select network. Widen iteration_q
independently of the two-bit state register. On the final iteration,
register quotient_step[2] and remainder_step[2]; on earlier iterations
register step[6]. Advance to CORRECT after iteration 5. Preserve all
33-bit trial subtraction and shifted-remainder widths. Do not run six
steps on the last iteration: processing 36 bits would corrupt both
quotient and remainder. No division or remainder operators are needed.

With the accepted request edge numbered 1, iteration edges are 2..7,
result_valid rises after correction edge 8, and result transfer can
occur on edge 9. Preserve this schedule in RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, using
the existing captured operands and exact XOR constants. Keep result
and result_valid stable under backpressure, reset cancellation, and
the existing once-only launch/transfer behavior. Signed truncation,
remainder sign, division by zero, and INT_MIN/-1 retain their existing
bit-exact behavior. The EX handshake already supports variable wait
duration and should need no functional change.

formal configuration triggers liveness at cycle 10 and requires the
next retirement by cycle 20. A simple four-step/eight-iteration design
with separate normalization and correction would create an eleven-cycle
adjacent-divide retirement interval. The proposed schedule instead has
a nine-cycle adjacent-divide interval, leaving one cycle for the
existing taken-branch or load-use bubble. Confirm these bounds with the
unmodified formal gates and directed pipeline cases; do not shorten
only the ALTOPS schedule or relax verification depths to obtain a pass.

The expected gain comes from reducing the measured recurrence from
eight to six serial subtract/select stages, with two extra blocking
clocks per DIV/REM. Keep the nret=1 interface, memory handshakes,

selection mux and a newly dominant multiplier or register-file path

title: Apply validated bimodal prediction to the clocked-divider champion
motivation:
The current champion still fetches sequentially and flushes on every
taken branch or jump. IF/ID is combinational, so each EX redirect wastes
one younger fetch slot, rather than the two implied by the stage names.
A predictor can remove this bubble without changing the arithmetic path.

LESSONS.md identifies the clocked divider as the source of the champion's
clock improvement; retain that implementation. The relevant predictor
experiment, hyp-20261001-003-r1s2, passed formal and cosimulation and cut
bracketed CoreMark cycles from 4,491,485 to 4,201,709, a 6.45 percent
reduction. Its regression label compares its 13.53 score against the
divider champion: its own critical path still crossed the old
combinational ALU, and its Fmax was only 5.685 MHz. This is evidence of a
useful predictor on the older parent, not a measurement of prediction
combined with the current 31.675 MHz clocked-divider parent. The current
champion also records 4,491,485 cycles, making this combination the most
directly supported predictor experiment.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a compact 64-entry bimodal direct-control-flow predictor to the
current RTL, preserving the existing clocked divider and pipeline depth.
Use two-bit saturating counters indexed by fetch PC[7:2], initialized to
weakly taken (2'b10). Predict a legal conditional branch taken when its
counter MSB is set; predict JAL taken unconditionally. Compute the target
from the current instruction's B or J immediate plus its full 32-bit PC.
Predict taken only when that target is word-aligned. All other encodings,
including JALR and reserved branch funct3 values, predict PC+4. This one
predictor uses no BTB, return stack, history register, or code-specific
addresses. Its small direction table avoids wide target/tag muxes.

Keep io_imemAddr driven directly by the existing PC register. Prediction
changes only the next registered PC; it must not create a combinational
instruction-memory address loop. Consume a prediction only when the
fetched instruction is actually accepted into ID/EX. Carry one
predicted_taken bit through if_id_t and id_ex_t with that instruction;
clear it on reset/flush and hold it with ID/EX during stalls. No predicted
target register is required because every predicted target is a direct
target that EX recomputes exactly from the same PC and immediate.

In EX, keep the architectural branch decision and resolved pc_next
separate from recovery. For direct BRANCH/JAL, recover only when
predicted_taken differs from the actual legal, aligned transfer decision.
A predicted-taken branch that resolves not taken recovers to its own
PC+4; a missed taken transfer recovers to the resolved target. Legal,
aligned JALR retains its existing EX redirect with target bit zero cleared.
Correct predictions never flush the fetched target instruction. Preserve
illegal-instruction and misalignment trap behavior, link PC+4, register
write suppression on faults, and linear next-PC behavior on a target
alignment fault. RVFI pc_next remains the actual architectural next PC,
never the prediction. Do not alter the decoder's default-illegal policy.

Recovery and counter training occur only on an EX acceptance event:
!reset && in.valid && !stall && !execute_wait. Train only legal conditional
branches without an alignment fault, using the resolving instruction's
PC[7:2] and actual outcome. Update the current addressed counter with
saturation, not a stale value saved at fetch. JAL/JALR, bubbles, and held
instructions do not train. Define simultaneous fetch lookup and training
to use the pre-edge counter value for the fetched prediction. EX checks
the captured prediction regardless of subsequent table aliasing.

Preserve all existing load-use, imem, dmem, and blocking-divide behavior.
During dmem stalls or execute_wait, hold PC and ID/EX prediction metadata
and defer recovery/training until EX can advance. A divide may complete
during a dmem stall; its result handshake and held operands remain intact.
When EX can advance, recovery must override an imem-not-ready PC hold,
squash the younger fetch, and install the corrected PC exactly once.
Under load-use bubbles or unavailable instruction data, consume no new
prediction. Preserve MEM/WB forwarding retention across dmem stalls and
prevent any wrong-path instruction from reaching a memory side effect.

Reproducing the prior cycle count at the champion's Fmax would improve
fitness by 6.90 percent, from 70.52 to approximately 75.38. Predict a
rounded 7 percent gain with medium confidence; this combined result is
unmeasured. Acceptance requires more than 73.76392. At 4,201,709 cycles,
Fmax must remain above approximately 30.995 MHz, allowing only about a
2.15 percent clock loss. The former predictor added 240 LUT4 relative to
its own baseline, but placement and fetch-target timing must be measured
again on this parent. Table aliasing, overlap with bus stalls, and a new
fetch-to-PC critical path are the principal risks. No divider or other
category changes should be added to rescue a failing predictor result.

Validate with directed pipeline tests, existing cocotb and formal gates,
and stalled cosimulation. Measure the unchanged marker-bracketed 2K
CoreMark run with canonical CRC and UART checks, then use median Gowin
Fmax times iterations/cycle for the acceptance decision. A local loop
timing test should demonstrate removal of the one-slot taken-branch
bubble after training; this is not a substitute for the fitness run.

title: Shorten divider trial subtraction with byte carry-select and borrow lookahead
motivation:
The champion scores 90.13 iterations/s at median Gowin Fmax 40.481 MHz.
Its worst reported path remains inside u_divider, from divisor_q to
remainder_q, with 194 cells and 30.694 ns reported arrival time. Six
dependent 33-bit trial subtractions and remainder selections occupy
each full restoring iteration. Optimizing this arithmetic feedback
path improves the clock for every instruction, including non-divides.

LESSONS.md and log.jsonl show that reducing eight restoring steps to
six improved fitness by 27.81 percent. The earlier fully combinational
radix-4 micro_opt reached only 5.749 MHz; the second round's structural
entry reproduced the six-step circuit and its score. Further increasing
divide latency risks the unchanged liveness check: the six-step design
already allows ten clocks between retirements when preceded by a
redirect or load-use bubble. Shortening each subtraction while retaining
this schedule targets the measured bottleneck without that latency risk.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace each of the six restoring steps' inferred full-width trial
subtraction with an explicit byte-partitioned carry-select subtractor
whose inter-byte borrows use parallel lookahead. Retain the restoring
algorithm, six-step unroll, five full iterations plus a final two-step
iteration, and all existing architectural and handshake behavior. This
is one local arithmetic micro-optimization, with no pipeline changes.

For each step let X = {remainder_step[i], quotient_step[i][31]} at
33 bits and D = divisor_q at 32 bits. For each byte k=0..3, independently
compute two explicitly unsigned nine-bit differences:
  T0[k] = {1'b0, X[8*k +: 8]} - {1'b0, D[8*k +: 8]}
  T1[k] = {1'b0, X[8*k +: 8]} - {1'b0, D[8*k +: 8]} - 9'd1.
Both candidates must be computed in parallel from the input bytes;
do not wait for the actual incoming borrow before doing subtraction.
Define G[k] = T0[k][8] and P[k] = (X_byte[k] == D_byte[k]).
G is the outgoing borrow with incoming borrow zero; P means an
incoming borrow propagates through an equal pair of bytes.

Compute byte-boundary borrows directly from these group signals:
  B0 = 0
  B1 = G0
  B2 = G1 | (P1 & G0)
  B3 = G2 | (P2 & G1) | (P2 & P1 & G0)
  B4 = G3 | (P3 & G2) | (P3 & P2 & G1) | (P3 & P2 & P1 & G0).
Use explicit balanced Boolean expressions for the lookahead, rather
than a serial chain of byte-borrow muxes. Select each result byte as
Bk ? T1[k][7:0] : T0[k][7:0]. Since the extended divisor's bit 32 is
zero, the original trial subtraction's bit 32 is X[32] XOR B4. Retain
that bit exactly: it controls selection of the old shifted remainder
versus the difference and supplies the complemented quotient bit.
Do not drop X[32], truncate trial candidates, infer signed arithmetic,
or replace this bit with B4 alone. The resulting trial vector must
equal the original 33-bit modular subtraction for every input pair.

Keep this helper local to rtl/divider.sv and instantiate or inline it
at each existing step using static generate indices. Use ordinary
synthesizable RTL accepted by Gowin and the formal frontend. The
intended dependency is an eight-bit local carry chain, a small group
borrow network, and byte selection, instead of a 33-bit carry chain
at every quotient bit. Do not add registers, duplicate the whole
divider, change the number of effective dividend shifts, or add
unrelated arithmetic, predictor, hazard, or register-file changes.

Preserve edge 1 capture/normalization, edges 2..7 iteration, edge 8
correction/result_valid, and earliest edge 9 result transfer. Keep
quotient/remainder selection, signed truncation toward zero, original
dividend remainder on division by zero, all-ones zero-divisor quotient,
INT_MIN/-1 handling, reset cancellation, and stable held completion.
Keep the RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas and identical control schedule;
the carry-select datapath belongs only in the real-arithmetic branch.
Preserve the nret=1 external interface and every existing invariant.

Predict a 20 percent fitness gain with medium confidence, from a
shorter divider feedback path and unchanged instruction-cycle counts.
This is unmeasured. Parallel byte candidates add arithmetic and mux
area, and Gowin may favor its native carry chain or move the critical
path to multiplication/forwarding. A successful implementation must
demonstrate the intended shorter path in vendor timing and exceed
94.27598 iterations/s, the champion times 1.046. With unchanged
4,491,485 bracketed cycles, the corresponding Fmax threshold is about
42.344 MHz. Use actual measured cycles and median Gowin Fmax to decide.

Validate subtraction equivalence independently of division, then run
real and ALTOPS ALU tests, existing pipeline and formal gates, stalled
cosimulation, and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART and marker checks. The
default ALTOPS proof does not validate the changed subtraction; real
arithmetic testing and an isolated combinational equivalence check
against X - {1'b0,D} are required evidence. Preserve all fixed formal
depths and liveness assertions and all existing latency checks.

micro-optimization and reached the same score. The earlier fully
combinational radix-4 attempt reached only 5.749 MHz: retaining clocked
state is essential. Replace the divider's recurrence architecture to

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rebuild the shared blocking DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU datapath as a clocked
unsigned radix-4 restoring divider surrounded by the existing signed
normalization and registered correction. Keep the external divider
handshake, EX integration, single-cycle non-divide operations, and
fixed eight-edge internal latency unchanged. Each main iteration
computes three radix-4 digits using three serial digit-selection
stages, instead of six serial binary subtract/select stages. Each
radix-4 stage evaluates subtraction of D, 2D, and 3D in parallel.

Avoid adding a setup cycle or placing computation of 3D in the feedback
chain. Capture normalized 32-bit dividend A and divisor D on request
edge 1. On iteration 0, edge 2, register the 34-bit multiple 3D from
zero-extended D plus zero-extended 2D, and simultaneously process only
the first two dividend bits using a separate small first-digit network.
With h=A[31:30], the first quotient digit and remainder are exactly:
D=1 gives q=h, r=0; D=2 gives q=h>>1, r=h&1; D=3 gives q=(h==3),
r=(h==3 ? 0 : h); D>=4 gives q=0, r=h. For D=0 choose q=3, r=h
as a deterministic internal convention; the existing exceptional-result
override supplies the architectural answer. Use D[31:2]==0 plus its
low two bits to decode this network. Register Q={A[29:0],q[1:0]} and
zero-extended r. Keep this first-digit logic separate from the reused
three-stage recurrence: there must be no combinational 3D bypass into
its subtractors, even on the preparation edge.

Iterations 1 through 5, edges 3 through 7, each consume three radix-4
digits using the registered D and 3D; 2D is just a widened shift of D.
This schedule consumes exactly 1+5*3=16 digits, or 32 dividend bits.
For each main digit form the 34-bit T={R[31:0],Q[31:30]}. Form unsigned
34-bit multiples D, 2D, and 3D without truncating their upper bits.
Compute three 35-bit trials {0,T}-{0,multiple} in parallel and use
bit 34 as the borrow flag. Select the largest non-borrowing digit
3, 2, or 1, otherwise select digit 0 and T. Generate mutually exclusive
digit enables and select the next remainder with a balanced masked-OR
network to avoid a serial three-way priority data mux. For D>0 the
selected remainder is below D and therefore fits in 32 bits; retain
those low 32 bits and append the two-bit quotient digit to Q. Do not
implement separate comparators followed by subtraction, or use / or %.

sign restoration, division-by-zero result, and INT_MIN/-1 handling.

the existing captured operands and constants. Retain once-only request
acceptance, stable held completion, reset cancellation, downstream
draining, saved RVFI operands, and the existing nine-cycle interval
between adjacent divides. The unchanged latency preserves the current
margin in the unmodified formal liveness window, including a preceding
load-use bubble or taken redirect. Preserve nret=1 and all IO, decoder,
memory, retirement, and arithmetic invariants.

The expected gain comes from halving dependent full-width subtract/select

carry propagation from the main recurrence. Three candidates per digit
increase subtractor area and divisor fanout, so Gowin routing and the
next-largest multiplier or forwarding path may limit the gain. The
expected 20 percent fitness improvement is an unmeasured hypothesis.

title: Combine proven bimodal prediction with the six-step-divider champion
motivation:
The current core fetches sequentially and flushes on every taken branch
or jump. IF/ID is combinational, so an EX redirect discards one younger
fetch slot. Removing these bubbles is a demonstrated opportunity even
with the benchmark's instruction and data bus stalls.

LESSONS.md and experiments/log.jsonl show that predictor experiments
hyp-20261001-003-r1s2 and hyp-20261001-003-r2s2 both passed formal and
cosimulation and reduced bracketed CoreMark cycles from 4,491,485 to
4,201,709, a 6.45 percent reduction. The latter scored 77.22 at 32.445 MHz
on the older eight-step-divider parent. Its regression against the
90.13 champion does not measure prediction on the six-step-divider core.
The current champion retains 4,491,485 cycles and reaches 40.481 MHz.
Combining the demonstrated cycle reduction with this existing clock
improvement is the most directly supported predictor experiment.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add the previously validated 64-entry bimodal direct-control-flow
predictor to the current six-step-divider RTL. This is one predictor
change: retain the current divider, ALU, forwarding, and pipeline depth.
Do not replace the current source with an earlier predictor snapshot
that would also restore its older arithmetic implementation.

Use 64 two-bit saturating counters indexed by fetch PC[7:2], reset to
weakly taken (2'b10). For a legal conditional BRANCH, predict taken when
the counter MSB is set. Predict JAL taken unconditionally. Form the
direct target from the full 32-bit fetch PC plus the instruction's
sign-extended B or J immediate. Permit taken predictions only for
word-aligned targets. Reserved BRANCH funct3 encodings, JALR, and all
other instructions predict PC+4. Use no target table, tags, return stack,
global history, benchmark-specific addresses, or instruction caching.

Keep io_imemAddr driven directly by the existing PC register. Consume
a prediction only when the fetched instruction is accepted into ID/EX:
no reset, recovery, fetch flush, or fetch stall. Prediction selects the
next registered PC and never creates a combinational instruction-memory
address loop. Carry one predicted_taken bit in if_id_t and id_ex_t;
capture it with the instruction, hold it through ID/EX stalls, and clear
it on reset or flush. A predicted-target register is unnecessary because
every predicted target is a direct target recomputed from the same
instruction and PC in EX.

Separate architectural control-flow resolution from recovery. In EX,
resolve the actual conditional outcome using the existing forwarded
operands. For BRANCH/JAL, redirect only when predicted_taken differs
from the actual legal, aligned transfer decision. A false taken
prediction recovers to that instruction's PC+4; a missed taken transfer
recovers to its resolved target. Legal aligned JALR retains EX recovery
with target bit zero cleared. Correct direct predictions cause no
flush, allowing the younger target instruction to enter ID/EX on the
edge where the branch advances. Preserve current misalignment traps,
illegal-instruction handling, JAL/JALR link values, write suppression
on faults, and linear next-PC behavior on a target alignment fault.
RVFI pc_next always reports the architectural resolved next PC.

Recovery and training must use an EX acceptance event:
!reset && in.valid && !stall && !execute_wait. Train only legal
conditional branches without an actual target-alignment fault, indexing
by the resolving instruction's PC[7:2] and saturating toward its actual
taken/not-taken outcome. Update the current table entry, not a counter
value saved at fetch. Concurrent lookup observes pre-edge counter state;
EX checks the captured prediction even if an alias changes the table.
Do not train JAL, JALR, invalid bubbles, or held instructions.

Retain the existing bus and execution interlocks. During a dmem stall,
hold PC and ID/EX metadata and defer recovery/training until EX advances.
During execute_wait, hold the younger fetch and the dividing instruction;
preserve divider request/result handshakes and retained launch operands.
Once EX advances, recovery overrides imem-not-ready and ordinary PC
holds, installs the corrected PC once, and squashes the younger slot.
Load-use bubbles and unavailable instruction data consume no prediction.
Keep MEM/WB forwarding data retained during dmem stalls. No wrong-path
register write, memory access, or retirement may escape recovery.
Preserve all top-level ports and the current nret=1 RVFI contract.

Reproducing 4,201,709 cycles at 40.481 MHz projects 96.34 iterations/sec,
approximately 6.9 percent above the 90.13 champion. Expected impact is
rounded to 7 percent with medium confidence; this combination has not
been measured. Acceptance requires more than 94.27598 iterations/sec.
At the projected cycle count, median Gowin Fmax must exceed about
39.612 MHz, allowing only about a 2.15 percent clock loss. The previous
predictor retained the divider as the critical path, but its routing
impact and the fetch target adder must be remeasured on this faster
parent. Table aliasing, bus-stall overlap, and placement effects remain
risks; do not assume a frequency gain or expand into arithmetic changes.

Validate with directed prediction and stall tests, existing cocotb and
formal gates, and stalled cosimulation. Demonstrate elimination of the
one-slot redirect bubble on a warm taken loop. Establish actual fitness
using the unchanged marker-bracketed 2K CoreMark run, canonical CRC and
UART validation, and median vendor Gowin Fmax. Local loop timing and
the projected score are not substitutes for this acceptance measurement.

title: Remove redirect-driven NOP mux from the fetch and decode datapath
motivation:
The champion scores 101.36 iterations/s at a median 45.526 MHz with
4,491,485 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path has moved
out of the divider: the 28.509 ns arrival traverses u_id, u_ex, u_if,
u_id/u_decoder, u_hazard, and returns to an ID operand register.
if_stage currently replaces imem_data with a NOP on redirect or an
instruction-bus stall. That late control therefore changes register
read addresses, decoder inputs, and load-use comparisons before the
ID/EX register can settle. This is unnecessary for killing an instruction.
LESSONS.md and the micro_opt log entries show successful divider depth
reduction, but the previous byte carry-select experiment regressed
to 24.392 MHz. Target the newly exposed control path instead of making
another speculative arithmetic mapping change.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Remove the combinational NOP substitution in if_stage and implement
fetch squashing only at the ID/EX register boundary. This is one local
control-path micro-optimization: retain the pipeline stages, branch
resolution cycle, redirect target, load-use bubble count, forwarding,
memory handshakes, and the existing eight-edge radix-4 divider.

Drive if_id.instr directly from imem_data on every cycle and if_id.pc
directly from the PC register. Keep if_id.valid deasserted on the same
redirect/flush conditions as today. No redirect, flush, or ready signal
may select instruction bits or register-file read addresses. The
decoder, immediate generator, and register reads operate on raw fetch
bits; their results only become executable when captured as valid.

In id_stage, preserve reset/flush priority, then stall/hold priority.
When the register is permitted to advance, capture the decoded payload
only if in.valid is true; otherwise install an invalid bubble with
ctrl entirely zero. Retain a deterministic all-zero bundle for bubbles
if convenient. Apply this kill at the destination register, never by
feeding a synthetic NOP back through decode. An unavailable fetch must
not clear a valid ID/EX instruction held for data-bus backpressure or
an outstanding divide. Clearing valid alone is insufficient: hazard
and forwarding logic also inspect control fields of invalid entries.

The hazard unit will now see raw instruction source fields. Qualify
its existing load-use comparison with imem_ready, independently of
redirect, so unavailable instruction data cannot create a load-use
stall. Keep the existing nonzero-rd check and raw rs1/rs2 comparisons;
do not add operand-use decoding as a second optimization. Do not gate
these addresses or this comparison with if_id.valid, because valid
includes the late redirect. A real load in ID/EX cannot simultaneously
be a resolving branch or jump; invalid ID/EX controls are zero. Thus
this qualification preserves the current effective load-use behavior
without a redirect-to-instruction-to-hazard dependency. Preserve the
current data-stall and execute-wait precedence over load-use bubbles,
and preserve redirect priority over instruction-bus stall at the PC.

Wrong-path or unavailable fetch words may decode as loads, stores,
divides, jumps, or illegal instructions, but must never enter ID/EX
with active controls or retire. Preserve the legal decoder defaults,
misalignment behavior, all RVFI fields for actual retirements, nret=1,
and the external ports. Do not register redirect, add a fetch stage,
change branch prediction, alter arithmetic, or optimize RVFI-only logic.

The expected benefit is removing a serial traversal of the fetch
instruction mux, read/decode logic, and hazard control after branch
resolution. The direct redirect-to-register squash path remains.
Instruction cycles should be unchanged; a 12 percent fitness gain
is an unmeasured prediction. Gowin may instead expose the divider,
multiplier, or another control path as the next clock limit.
Run the unchanged unit, formal, and cosimulation gates, canonical
CoreMark UART/CRC/marker checks with the specified bus stalls, and
median Gowin timing. Compare the actual bracketed cycle count and
confirm that the old redirect-through-decode path disappears.
Acceptance requires measured fitness above 106.02256, or more than
47.620196 MHz if cycles remain exactly unchanged.

title: Separate pipeline kill control from the fetch and decode payload
motivation:
The champion scores 101.36 iterations/s at 45.526 MHz with 4,491,485
bracketed cycles. Its reported worst path now starts in the register
file and ends at ID/EX rs1_val, traversing ID, EX, IF, decode, and hazard
logic: 28.509 ns arrival and 51 cells. LESSONS.md and the structural
history show that clocking division and replacing its recurrence with
radix-4 removed the previous arithmetic bottleneck. Further divider
changes would miss the new reported limiting path.

IF currently substitutes an entire NOP instruction on a late EX redirect
or unavailable fetch. That substitution changes decoder inputs, source
addresses, register-file reads, immediates, and load-use comparisons.
ID then also clears its entire wide payload on a flush. This couples
branch resolution back through instruction decode and operand selection
within one clock. Separating transaction validity from payload movement
directly targets that unnecessary structural dependency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the existing IF-to-ID/EX boundary into an independently
moving data payload and a small bubble-control path, without adding a
pipeline stage or changing instruction latencies. Drive IF's instruction
field directly from imem_data, even on redirects and unavailable-fetch
cycles. Continue driving the current PC. Keep redirect priority over PC
stalls and use the existing fetch-valid indication to mark discarded
instructions. The raw instruction, decoder, immediate generator, source
addresses, and register-file read muxes must have no combinational
dependence on redirect, flush, or fetch-valid.

Split ID/EX updates by purpose. Reset still initializes the full bundle.
On every non-stalled edge, capture PC, instruction, immediate, register
indices, and register-file operand values independently of flush and
incoming valid. On flush clear only the registered ctrl bundle and valid,
with the same flush-over-stall priority as today. Otherwise, when ID is
allowed to advance, set valid from incoming valid and set ctrl to the
decoded control only for a valid input, or to all zeros for a bubble.
A held instruction retains all its fields. Thus payload bits in a bubble
are defined but irrelevant, and a killed instruction cannot assert a
memory, register-write, branch, jump, or divide control. Do not implement
this by masking the raw instruction or source addresses earlier in the
cone, or by zeroing the wide payload on a flush.

Derive load-use dependencies from the raw fetch source fields and the
registered ID/EX load destination. Qualify them with imem_ready, which
is the bus availability indication, rather than the redirect-dependent
IF valid signal. Retain the current conservative comparison of both
instruction source bitfields; semantic source-use optimization is outside
this hypothesis. A redirect still flushes the younger instruction and
overrides fetch hold. Preserve dmem-stall and execute-wait precedence:
they hold ID/EX, dmem stalls preserve EX/MEM requests, and a load-use
bubble clears control while allowing the older load to advance.

Keep the existing EX behavior that emits a completely cleared EX/MEM
bubble for an invalid input or a waiting divide. This local control
separation must not turn into a global change of forwarding validity:
MEM/WB intentionally retains data and forwarding eligibility after its
retirement-valid bit clears during a dmem stall. Preserve that behavior,
the once-only divider launch/transfer protocol, saved divider RVFI
operands, and the current eight-edge real/ALTOPS divider schedule.
Retain the decoder's default-illegal policy and all existing traps.
Preserve nret=1, every top-level port, memory handshakes, and strict
retirement ordering. Invalid payloads must never reach RVFI retirement
or cause architectural side effects.

This is one structural pipeline-control refactoring: remove the
EX-redirect-to-instruction-to-decode/register-read dependency while
terminating kill decisions at the registered control boundary. It
should preserve the accepted instruction schedule and CoreMark cycles
while increasing Fmax. Predict a 15 percent fitness gain with medium
confidence; this is unmeasured. A remaining divider or multiplier path,
control fanout, or vendor synthesis merging may limit the gain.

Run existing unit tests, unmodified formal and stalled cosimulation
gates, and the canonical CoreMark CRC, UART, and marker checks. Inspect
Gowin timing to verify removal of the redirect-driven decode/read path
and measure the new limiting path. Acceptance requires measured median
Fmax times iterations/cycle above 106.02256 iterations/s, which is
101.36 times 1.046. Use measured bracketed cycles; unchanged 4,491,485
cycles would require approximately 47.62 MHz. Do not relax formal
depths, latency assertions, or any evaluation contract.

only for a real ID stall and resets deterministically; flush and

title: Bimodal prediction with recovery isolated from fetch decode
motivation:
The current radix-4-divider champion still fetches sequentially and
discards one younger fetch slot on every taken branch or jump. IF/ID
is combinational, so there is one redirect bubble despite the nominal
five-stage description. LESSONS.md and the three predictor experiments
hyp-20261001-003-r1s2, hyp-20261001-003-r2s2, and hyp-20261001-003-r3s2
establish a repeatable opportunity: a 64-entry bimodal direct predictor
passed formal and cosimulation and reduced bracketed CoreMark cycles
from 4,491,485 to 4,201,709, a 6.45 percent reduction. The last attempt
scored 94.47 at 39.693 MHz on the older six-step binary-divider parent;
it did not measure prediction on the present 45.526 MHz radix-4 core.

The current champion scores 101.36, and its reported worst path runs
from register-file data through EX, IF, ID decode, and the hazard unit
back to ID/EX. The source exposes the relevant avoidable dependency:
EX redirect selects a NOP in IF before decode and source-address hazard
comparisons. Prediction recovery should kill the younger instruction
at the pipeline register boundary, without first changing the data
being decoded. Integrating the proven predictor this way targets its
cycle savings while protecting the now-critical recovery path.

title: Separate the memory address register from the general ALU result
motivation:
The champion scores 113.55 iterations/s at 47.710 MHz with 4,201,709
bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md and the recent micro_opt history
show that clocking division and removing the redirect-to-decode path
exposed a different bottleneck. A fresh vendor timing run reproduces
the champion's placement-0 result of 50.031 MHz and its 25.282 ns
worst-path arrival. The detailed path crosses register-file output,
operand muxes, a DSP multiplier, ALU result selection, and the data
RAM address input. In the RTL, EX/MEM.alu_result supplies both integer
results and every memory-address consumer, although a load/store
address needs only forwarded rs1 plus its immediate. This unnecessary
sharing makes the general arithmetic result network part of address
timing. Prior byte carry-select division regressed badly; the proposed
change targets the measured address path without changing arithmetic.

not a new stage, memory protocol, or execution schedule.

operation/result mux. The intended synthesis result is that multiplier,

title: Register and share multiplication behind a blocking EX handshake
motivation:
The champion scores 113.55 iterations/s at median 47.71 MHz and
4,201,709 bracketed cycles. LESSONS.md and structural experiments
r1s1 through r4s1 establish that divider staging and removing the
recovery dependency already improved the clock. No prior recorded
structural experiment stages multiplication, which still has three
live full-width product expressions in the ordinary EX datapath.

A fresh unchanged-core Gowin option-0 run reproduces 50.031 MHz and
the reported 25.282 ns worst-path arrival. The detailed path launches
from register-file BSRAM, crosses ID operand correction and EX
forwarding, traverses multiplier DSP mult_5_s1, then passes through
ALU selection to the data-memory BRAM. A branch-recovery path is nearly
tied at 25.269 ns, so isolated DSP delay is not the entire opportunity.
Capturing multiply operands and sharing the three products removes
the forwarded-input multiply cone and reduces DSP and operand-routing
pressure. It charges additional cycles only to multiply instructions.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement MUL, MULH, MULHU, and MULHSU with one shared clocked
multiplier inside alu.sv. Put an operand register before the product
and a 32-bit architectural-result register after it, integrated with
EX's existing blocking execution protocol. Keep all base operations
single-cycle, preserve the current radix-4 divider schedule, and
retain the existing predictor and pipeline topology. This is one
structural change to the multiply execution boundary.

Use IDLE, COMPUTE, and DONE states. req_ready is true only in IDLE.
On accepted request edge 1, capture the operation and two signed
33-bit operands from the exact forwarded input values. A's extra bit
is a[31] for MULH or MULHSU and zero otherwise. B's extra bit is b[31]
for MULH and zero otherwise. Thus MUL/MULHU use unsigned magnitudes,
MULH uses two signed values, and MULHSU uses signed A and unsigned B.
Compute one signed 33-by-33 product with an explicit 66-bit result;
do not truncate operands or multiply at 32-bit expression width.

On edge 2, register product[31:0] for the captured MUL operation or
product[63:32] for the other three operations, and enter DONE. Bits
65:64 are not architectural result bits. Assert result_valid in DONE,
with the registered result held until result_ready accepts it.
Earliest EX/MEM result transfer is edge 3. The state then returns to
IDLE; a subsequent multiply launches as a new transaction. Forwarded
live operands must end at the input registers, and the old three
combinational multiply expressions must disappear. Ordinary ALU
output selection sees only the registered multiply result. Reset
clears state and registers and cancels any pending transaction.

Add a separate multiply request/completion interface alongside the
existing divider interface. In EX, recognize only the four multiply
ALU operations. Launch when in.valid && is_multiply && !stall &&
mul_req_ready. Assert multiply result_ready only for the held valid
multiply when !stall. Extend execute_wait to cover a valid multiply
without a valid result, OR the existing divide wait. The existing
hazard unit then holds fetch and ID/EX while older MEM/WB work drains.
Preserve dmem-stall priority: hold an older EX/MEM memory request;
otherwise install a fully cleared EX/MEM bubble while execution waits.
Transfer the completed multiply into EX/MEM exactly once and resume
ordinary forwarding to its immediate consumer on the following cycle.

Capture both original post-forwarding source values on multiply
launch for RVFI, just as division already does. The same saved-source
pair can serve multiply and divide because EX permits only one active
blocking operation. Use these saved values at retirement, not live
forwarding sources that may have drained. Keep divide and multiply
ready/valid controls distinct; alternating operations must not reuse
stale results or launch twice. Invalid or squashed fetches must not
start multiplication, write memory, train prediction, or retire.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS preserve this exact edge-1 capture, edge-2
result, earliest-edge-3 transfer schedule. On edge 2 use captured
32-bit operands and the original formulas: MUL=(a+b)^0x5876063e,
MULH=(a+b)^0xf6583fb7, MULHU=(a+b)^0x949ce5e8, and
MULHSU=(a-b)^0xecfbe137, all modulo 2^32. Exclude the real multiplier
from the ALTOPS arithmetic cone. Do not change divider arithmetic or
latency, legality decoding, traps, memory handshakes, nret=1 IO,
contiguous retirement ordering, or the existing verification gates.

A disposable prototype of precisely this ALU/EX change produced
Gowin Fmax values 54.346, 56.523, and 56.523 MHz across placement
options 0, 1, and 2: median 56.523 MHz. Its option-0 resources were
3,678 LUTs, 833 flip-flops, and 2 DSPs, versus 3,630/794/6 for the
champion. Its worst reported path moved into the divider recurrence.
The unchanged CoreMark validator accepted all canonical CRCs, UART,
bounds, completion, and timing brackets at 4,389,122 cycles for ten
iterations under the usual instruction/data stalls. This is 4.46
percent more cycles but 18.47 percent higher median Fmax, projecting
128.7797 iterations/s, a 13.41 percent fitness gain. All 22 existing
pipeline tests and the 115-retirement stalled selftest cosimulation
also passed. With a handshake-adapted helper retaining the existing
arithmetic vectors, all 30 ALU tests passed in both real-arithmetic
and ALTOPS builds, including captured-operand and held-result checks.
These are preliminary prototype results, not a completed
orchestrator acceptance or a substitute for formal verification.

Implement the same register boundaries and validate real arithmetic,
held completion, reset cancellation, and the matching ALTOPS schedule.
Run all unchanged formal and stalled cosimulation gates plus canonical
CoreMark and all Gowin placement options. Acceptance requires fitness
above 118.7733 iterations/s; at the prototype's measured cycle count
this requires median Fmax above 52.1311 MHz. The next divider-limited
path, changed placement, and dynamic multiply frequency are remaining
risks. The expected net improvement is 13 percent with medium
confidence, grounded in the prototype rather than an assumed IPC.

title: Reset-independent bimodal prediction with configuration-time initialization
motivation:
LESSONS.md and previous predictor attempts establish that the existing
64-entry bimodal BRANCH/JAL predictor saves useful bubbles. The r4s2
champion scores 113.55 iterations/sec at 47.71 MHz and 4,201,709
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Preserve that policy and recovery integration.

Architectural trace replay estimates only 51,854 conditional direction
misses in the measured region. A 512-entry table removes only about
12,000 of these, far below the cycle savings needed for acceptance.
Predictor implementation cost is the stronger opportunity. Every
counter currently participates in synchronous reset, although its
contents are advisory and EX verifies every direct prediction.

An isolated prototype initializes the existing table at configuration
and retains it across runtime reset. It preserves exactly 4,201,709
bracketed cycles. Unmodified Gowin evaluation reports placement-option
Fmax values 48.372, 50.467, and 50.467 MHz, with median 50.467 MHz.
LUT4 falls from 3,630 to 3,440; FF remains 794 and LUT-RAM remains 8.
The measured benefit is removal of reset-related logic and improved
physical implementation, not a RAM conversion or accuracy improvement.

title: Use distributed register storage with validity-gated read selection
motivation:
The champion scores 129.31 iterations/s at 54.331 MHz and 4,201,709
bracketed CoreMark cycles. A fresh Gowin run reproduced its 25.514 ns
worst path starting at the register-file BSRAM output and traversing
operand selection and branch recovery. The recent micro_opt history
shows that separating effective addresses exposed this path without
adding cycles; the blocking multiplier lost throughput to extra waits.
The present 32-by-32 register array has a bulk synchronous reset and
is mapped into block RAM with absorbed operand registers. A local
storage/reset rewrite can restore a faster ID/EX launch boundary
while preserving the exact architectural register-file interface.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement the same 32-register, two-asynchronous-read, single-write
register file with distributed RAM storage and a small resettable
written bitmap. Remove only the bulk reset assignment to the 32-bit
data words. Apply the Gowin synthesis attribute
(* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *) to the regs array, retaining
portable behavioral RTL for simulation and formal verification.
Keep one synchronous data write when !reset && w_en && w_addr!=0.

Reset written_q to zero; every accepted nonzero-register write sets
written_q[w_addr]. Each read retains the original priority: x0 reads
zero; a matching enabled write bypasses w_data; otherwise return the
stored word only when that register's written bit is set, and zero
when it is clear. Preserve the original bypass behavior even during
reset rather than silently changing the combinational interface.
Implement each read with two mutually exclusive masked data terms:
bypass = w_en && w_addr==r_addr && r_addr!=0;
stored = !bypass && written_q[r_addr] && r_addr!=0;
r_data = ({32{bypass}} & w_data) | ({32{stored}} & regs[r_addr]).
This combines zero/reset validity with source qualification before
the data OR, avoiding cascaded wide zero/bypass muxes.

Reset suppresses data writes and clears validity, so stale RAM words
cannot leak after reset. Every valid word must have been written
since the most recent reset. Never assume uninitialized RAM is zero.

operand registers, eliminating the block-RAM output as the launch
point of the long EX arithmetic/recovery paths. Verify this mapping
in the vendor report; the attribute alone is not evidence of success.

title: Peel four dividend bits at launch and shorten the divider recurrence
motivation:
The champion scores 129.31 iterations/s at median 54.331 MHz and
4,201,709 bracketed CoreMark cycles. A fresh unchanged-core Gowin run
reproduces its 25.514 ns branch-recovery path and a nearly tied
25.480 ns divider feedback path. Earlier structural divider staging
produced large gains without changing measured CoreMark cycles.
Three serial radix-4 digit selections still occupy each feedback
cycle. Shortening this recurrence must preserve the original latency:
an extra divide cycle fails the unchanged load-dependent liveness bound.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition the shared divider without changing its eight internal
clocks or earliest edge-9 result transfer. On request edge 1 normalize
signed operands, process the first FOUR dividend bits with a small
leading-digit network, and register the full 34-bit 3D multiple.
On edges 2 through 8 reuse TWO full-width radix-4 restoring stages per
clock. This consumes exactly 4 + 7*4 = 32 dividend bits. In DONE expose
sign correction from stable final quotient/remainder registers to the
existing EX/MEM acceptance register; remove the separate CORRECT state
and corrected-result register. This is one divider-boundary change.

Let A and D denote normalized 32-bit magnitudes and h=A[31:28]. The
launch network computes q_head=floor(h/D) and r_head=h-q_head*D.
Define head_d=(D[31:4]!=0) ? 0 : D[3:0]. Use a combinational
256-entry constant truth table indexed by {head_d,h}, with each
eight-bit entry equal to {q_head,r_head}. Map divisor code zero to
{4'b0,h}; this also represents D>=16, whose head quotient is zero
and remainder is h. Select this bypass at the lookup ADDRESS, not
with another mux after its outputs. Generate
the entries at authoring time; use literal case entries in synthesizable
RTL, not runtime division operators. For D=0 encode {4'b0,h}; the
captured zero flag overrides completion. This table replaces serial
small-divider arithmetic on the already-late launch operand path.
Full-width D must determine head_d; using only low divisor bits
without the upper-bit check would corrupt divisors of 16 or greater.
Do not truncate the full divisor used by subsequent iterations. D=0
uses deterministic head values because the captured zero flag
overrides the final architectural result. Avoid full-width / or %.
Register quotient_q={A[27:0],q_head} and remainder_q={28'b0,r_head}
at launch, alongside normalized D, 34-bit 3D, original dividend,
quotient/remainder sign flags, operation selection, zero and overflow.
Compute 3D from D with explicitly widened D + (D<<1), not a 32-bit sum.

Keep only two dependent full-width radix-4 stages. Each computes
parallel unsigned trial differences against registered D, 2D, and 3D,
then selects the largest fitting multiple with one-hot masks. Preserve
34-bit shifted dividends and 35-bit trial differences with borrow bit
34. For iteration indices 0..6, register quotient_step[2] and
remainder_step[2]; enter DONE after index 6. Processing fourteen more
radix-4 digits after the two at launch consumes exactly sixteen digits.

In DONE, result_valid is high and result is combinational sign
correction/selection of quotient_q or remainder_q, with the captured
divide-by-zero and signed-overflow overrides. Do not correct the live
iteration outputs: correction starts at the stable state registers.
Keep all these registers and flags unchanged while DONE is blocked,
so result stays stable until result_ready. EX/MEM captures it on edge
9 at the earliest. Reset cancels pending work; consume once and return
to IDLE only on acceptance. Preserve signed truncation toward zero,
remainder sign, INT_MIN/-1, and all four division operations exactly.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS capture the original operands/op at request,
run the same seven iteration clocks, and expose the original four
XOR formulas in DONE with the identical edge-9 transfer schedule.
Preserve EX's once-only request/completion protocol, saved RVFI source
values, downstream draining, memory-hold priority, and full bubbles.
Keep multiplication, ordinary ALU operations, prediction, effective
memory addresses, nret=1 IO, legality, traps and retirement order intact.
Do not alter any formal depth, liveness bound, or existing exact-latency
assertion. Keep the current two-bit state encoding with IDLE=0,
ITERATE=1 and DONE=3; the unused CORRECT encoding need not be retained
as a functional state.

Target a 6 percent fitness gain with low confidence before final
evaluation. The intended gain comes from two digit selections between
feedback registers and moving correction to the existing EX/MEM
register. Input normalization plus the head truth table and 3D
preparation, and remaining branch/multiply paths, are timing risks.
Run unchanged unit and formal gates, real and ALTOPS arithmetic tests,
stalled reference cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/
marker validation. Measure all three Gowin placement options and actual
bracketed cycles; acceptance requires more than 135.25826 iterations/s.

Preliminary evidence: the latency-preserving schedule passed all 53
unchanged ALTOPS formal checks. The constant-table prototype with an
OUTPUT bypass mux passed the existing real/ALTOPS ALU and pipeline
tests, eight stalled/unstalled reference-cosimulation cases, and all
CoreMark validation at exactly 4,201,709 cycles. Its Gowin options were
56.565/54.599/54.599 MHz, below the required improvement. The proposed
address-side bypass removes that extra lookup-output mux, but a score
above the acceptance threshold is not yet established. Do not claim
success from the faster option alone. Remaining multiplier paths and
placement sensitivity make this a deliberately low-confidence proposal.

title: Bypass completed loads directly to branch comparison without an interlock bubble
motivation: The champion scores 136.42 iterations/s at 57.319 MHz and 4,201,709 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior micro_opt wins removed unnecessary dependencies without adding execution latency. Fresh isolated mux, multiplier-sharing, and divider simplification experiments did not improve median timing on this parent. A branch-only load bypass instead removes a real instruction bubble while keeping memory data outside the multiplier/general ALU operand cone. A prototype reduced CoreMark to 4,064,795 cycles, a 3.26 percent cycle reduction, and passed canonical validation and reference cosimulation. This makes load-to-branch interlocking the most promising tested throughput opportunity.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a MEM-to-EX bypass exclusively for conditional-branch comparison and eliminate the load-use bubble only when the fetched instruction is a legal conditional branch. Preserve the existing pipeline stages, retirement width, prediction policy, operation latencies, and both memory handshakes. Do not bypass loads into the general ALU or multiplier, and do not remove interlocks for arithmetic, stores, or JALR.

In mem_stage expose the existing sign/zero-extended load_data and a branch_load_valid qualifier equal to in.valid && in.ctrl.mem_read && ctrl_with_trap.reg_write. Thus LB/LBU/LH/LHU/LW use their exact architectural values and misaligned loads cannot advertise a result. Route these signals and the EX/MEM destination tag to ex_stage. For each branch comparison operand, select branch_load_data when branch_load_valid, destination is nonzero, and its tag matches that source; otherwise select the existing forwarded rs value. Use these two new values only in all six conditional-branch comparisons and the branch's captured RVFI source values. Leave alu_a, alu_b, effective-address generation, store data, divider launch values, and jump-target generation on their existing operands.

Prevent a load's effective address from masquerading as register data on the ordinary EX/MEM forwarding path. Add a single forward_alu_valid bit to ex_mem_t. Capture ctrl_with_trap.reg_write && !ctrl_with_trap.mem_read alongside the accepted EX instruction, clear it with existing reset/bubble clears, and retain it through data-memory holds. Use this REGISTERED bit as forward_unit's EX/MEM write eligibility. Retain the existing destination-zero check, tag comparison, EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority, and MEM/WB forwarding without valid gating. In particular, a faulting load must leave a dependent branch reading the prior architectural value via retained WB or ID/EX data; forwarding its address is incorrect. Registering eligibility avoids inserting a new mem_read gate on the timed EX forwarding path.

In hazard_unit qualify the load-use interlock with !if_id_branch. Compute if_id_branch directly from the raw fetch word: opcode 0x63 and funct3 neither 2 nor 3. Keep imem_ready, valid, nonzero destination, source comparisons, and every other hazard term. A stalled older memory operation still freezes EX/MEM and the dependent branch in ID/EX. EX's existing ex_accept already forbids redirect, training, or branch transfer until that memory operation can advance. On the ready edge the load enters MEM/WB and the branch enters EX/MEM using its completed data, with normal in-order retirement. Preserve redirect priority, once-only training, misaligned target handling, wrong-path squash, and all decoder legality defaults.

This is one local forwarding/interlock optimization, not a new predictor or memory architecture. All addresses remain full width; retain nret=1, every top-level port, all ALTOPS and real M arithmetic, division completion timing, contiguous RVFI order, canonical CoreMark checks, and all unchanged formal gates.

Preliminary evidence for the branch-only bypass with combinational non-load forwarding qualification: all 26 existing pipeline tests passed, the standard cosimulation evaluator passed five ELFs including stalled CoreMark validation, and the benchmark completed in 4,064,795 bracketed cycles. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 54.665/55.350/55.350 MHz, giving approximately 136.169 iterations/s, below the champion and below acceptance. That prototype establishes the cycle benefit, NOT a fitness improvement. The final proposal registers the forwarding qualifier as described above to protect the general ALU path. Its timing must be measured separately. Expected gain is deliberately low-confidence because divider feedback and physical routing may still dominate.

Retain all existing tests and add directed load-to-branch tests with dependencies on either or both sources, every load width/sign mode, all six branch predicates, x0, youngest-writer priority, and misaligned loads following an older writer of the same register. Exercise independent long bus stalls, ready-edge release, mispredictions, reset, and wrong-path/invalid fetches. Check exact RVFI source data, PCs, order, trap handling, stable outstanding memory requests, and once-only retirement/training. Add cycle assertions proving the no-wait load-to-branch pair loses its former bubble while ALU/store/JALR consumers still interlock. Run the unchanged full formal and cosimulation gates; preliminary simulation is not a formal proof. Acceptance requires measured fitness above 142.69532 iterations/s, approximately 58.005 MHz at the prototype cycle count, using the actual final cycles and median Fmax.

title: Decouple fetch with a four-entry fall-through instruction queue
motivation:
The champion scores 136.42 iterations/s at 57.319 MHz with 4,201,709
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its fetch PC currently advances only when
decode accepts the instruction. Load-use bubbles, blocking divides
and data-memory stalls therefore waste otherwise-ready fetch cycles,
despite independent instruction backpressure on roughly 22 percent
of cycles. Structural attempt hyp-20261001-002-r5s1 paid 4.46 percent
more cycles for registered multiplication, while hyp-20261001-002-r6s1
lost fitness after shortening the divider. LESSONS.md shows diminishing
returns from arithmetic staging as other EX paths become limiting.
A small elastic queue targets wasted fetch opportunities and cycles.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 136.42 iterations/s at 57.319 MHz with 4,201,709
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its fetch PC currently advances only when
decode accepts the instruction. Load-use bubbles, blocking divides
and data-memory stalls therefore waste otherwise-ready fetch cycles,
despite independent instruction backpressure on roughly 22 percent
of cycles. Structural attempt hyp-20261001-002-r5s1 paid 4.46 percent
more cycles for registered multiplication, while hyp-20261001-002-r6s1
lost fitness after shortening the divider. LESSONS.md shows diminishing
returns from arithmetic staging as other EX paths become limiting.
A small elastic queue targets wasted fetch opportunities and cycles.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert a four-entry fall-through instruction queue inside if_stage.
Separate the speculative fetch PC from the PC of the oldest instruction
presented to decode. Keep the existing direct BRANCH/JAL predictor and
train it from accepted EX branches exactly as before. Fetch computes
its next predicted PC and advances whenever a ready bus word can be
consumed directly or enqueued, independently of downstream load-use,
divide and data-memory holds. Each queue entry stores the complete
instruction, its own PC and the prediction actually used at fetch.
Decode and RVFI must use the head entry's PC, never the advanced fetch PC.

Use a four-entry circular buffer, two-bit read/write pointers and a
three-bit occupancy count. Store one full 66-bit if_id_t packet per
entry. Use if_id_t entries [0:3] for Gowin/Verilator. The Yosys frontend
loses the unpacked array dimension on this struct typedef, producing
an actual pc_fwd failure. Under its predefined YOSYS macro declare
logic [65:0] entries [0:3] instead. This is solely a frontend syntax
workaround: identical packed field order, 66-bit width, four entries,
and bit-for-bit shared read/write/valid/pointer/control expressions.
Do not branch on FORMAL/ALTOPS or substitute behavioral logic. Test
both declarations in simulation against the same architectural traces
and queue scoreboard; formal must analyze the complete four-entry FIFO.
Gowin's plain-vector declaration maps differently and measured only
52.686 MHz, so preserve the vendor's measured struct-array declaration.
Empty queue output bypasses the live bus
word and imemReady, preserving the current zero-extra-cycle path.
Nonempty output comes from the oldest registered entry and remains
valid even while io_imemReady is low. Define consume as head-valid
and decode-can-accept. With no redirect/reset, dequeue is consume
and count!=0; fetch_accept is io_imemReady and (count<4 or dequeue);
enqueue is fetch_accept and (count!=0 or !consume). Empty bypass
consumption advances fetch PC without touching occupancy or pointers.
Otherwise capture on enqueue, advance the write pointer, and advance
the read pointer on dequeue. Update count by enqueue minus dequeue.
At full occupancy permit simultaneous dequeue/enqueue; decode must
see the old head while the edge writes the replacement. No packet
may be dropped, duplicated or overwritten while blocked.

Reinterpret the existing fetch stall as a block on head consumption,
not a blanket freeze of the fetch producer. In core.sv feed queued
head validity, rather than raw io_imemReady, to the hazard unit's
instruction-availability input. Preserve the existing load-use source
comparisons on the presented head instruction, ID/EX hold/bubble
priorities and all dmem/divider control. Thus a ready queued head can
advance while the external instruction bus stalls, and a blocked head
can accumulate additional predicted-path words while space remains.
When the queue is full and cannot dequeue, hold io_imemAddr stable.

Accepted EX recovery overrides all queue and bus activity: set fetch
PC to redirect_target and invalidate the entire queue on that edge,
with no enqueue/dequeue accepted. The existing ID/EX flush kills the
presented younger instruction. This also works when imemReady is zero
or the queue is full. Reset clears occupancy and pointers, resets PC
and predictor as before, and need not reset invalid queue payloads.
Wrong-path prefetches have no architectural effects and must never
retire, train, launch a divide, or access data memory. Preserve the
exact nret=1 ports, precise single retirement and +1 order sequence,
decoder legality, RV32M arithmetic/ALTOPS, memory bounds and handshakes.
This proposal changes front-end elasticity only: no cache, predictor
policy change, arithmetic redesign, or extra pipeline stage.

Expect a 7 percent net fitness gain with medium confidence. Fetch-run-ahead may hide independent bus stalls during
existing execution bubbles, while empty fall-through avoids adding a
fixed recovery or instruction latency. A new head-selection mux and
wider predicted-path buffering can affect timing and wrong-path traffic;
the queue may also remain empty when fetch bandwidth is the bottleneck.
Measure actual canonical CoreMark cycles and all three Gowin options.
Require fitness above 142.69532 iterations/s, with the unchanged five
CRCs, UART success literal, in-bounds accesses and MMIO timing markers.
Run the existing unit, formal and stalled reference-cosimulation gates
without weakening bounds, assumptions or architectural assertions.
A disposable prototype of this exact four-entry circular, fall-through
structure completed canonical stalled CoreMark in 3,977,318 bracketed
cycles versus 4,201,709, a 5.34 percent cycle reduction. The unchanged
validator passed all CRC/UART/bounds/completion/marker checks. Gowin
placement options 0/1/2 measured 56.359/58.222/58.222 MHz, for a median
of 58.222 MHz. Their product projects 146.3851 iterations/s, 7.30 percent
above 136.42 and above the 142.69532 acceptance threshold. Option-0
resources were 4,094 logic cells, 813 FFs, 49 LUT-RAM, four BSRAM and
six DSPs. The worst paths remain EX arithmetic and divider recurrence.
Preserve the circular representation and unreset payload storage used
by this prototype; changing to a shifting flop queue is not measured.

All 26 existing pipeline tests and an added FIFO stress test passed
with both packet declarations after retaining their complete
architectural assertions and adapting the predictor observer to model
a software FIFO separately from speculative fetch PC. The check that
a stalled branch cannot redirect remains; speculative fetch may now
continue while it waits. The added test checks full occupancy, full
simultaneous enqueue/dequeue, consumption with imemReady low, full-queue
redirect, exact retirements, and suppression of wrong-path divides and
stores. Full reference cosimulation passed selftest plus three random
programs with and without bus stalls; canonical CoreMark validation
passed again with the plain-vector declaration at identical cycles.
With the corrected four-entry storage, all 53 unchanged ALTOPS formal
checks passed, including pc_fwd, liveness and reg_ch0. An explicit
YOSYS-defined Verilator build also passed all 27 pipeline tests. The
final source with the declaration workaround reproduced exactly
56.359/58.222/58.222 MHz across Gowin's three placement options.
These are prototype results, not completed orchestrator acceptance;
reproduce all unchanged correctness and timing gates in implementation.
At this measured cycle count acceptance
requires median Fmax above 56.75447 MHz.
