title: Carry fetch-computed direct targets into predictor recovery
motivation:
The champion already predicts BRANCH/JAL with a 64-entry bimodal table.
Prior trace replay estimates only 51,854 conditional misses among
4,201,709 measured cycles, and fresh profiling finds just 13,735 JALRs.
Accuracy expansion alone therefore has little headroom to clear the
required 4.6 percent fitness gain. Prior reset-retention wins were on
other parents; local trials of counter implementations, delayed training
and recovery Boolean factoring all regressed on this champion.

Fetch already computes a full direct target and PC+4 for next-PC
prediction, but EX recomputes both from the registered PC and immediate.
Moving these existing results with the prediction offers a different
opportunity: remove duplicated adders from recovery and the jump-link
result path while preserving every prediction decision and cycle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Extend the existing direct predictor's metadata with two full-width
values: direct_target, computed in IF from the current instruction's
B/J immediate, and fallthrough_pc, computed as current PC+4. Carry
both through if_id_t into id_ex_t alongside predicted_taken. Capture
them only with an accepted instruction; hold them with the entire
ID/EX payload during stalls and clear them on reset or bubbles.
These are instruction-derived addresses, not a tagged target cache.

Reuse the arithmetic already present in if_stage: name the existing
PC+4 expression once as fallthrough_pc, keep the existing direct_imm
and direct_target computation, and export both values. Do not add
another target adder, table, prediction stage, bypass or fetch slot.
Continue driving imem_addr from the PC register and preserve the
current prediction, alignment gating and correction priority.

In EX, use the captured direct_target for a decoded conditional
branch and for direct JAL. JALR still computes forwarded rs1+imm
and clears bit zero exactly as before. Replace every architectural
EX PC+4 use with captured fallthrough_pc: jump link result, linear
resolved next PC, trap continuation and not-taken recovery target.
Retain the original PC for AUIPC, RVFI pc_rdata and predictor training
index. Keep the original immediate for arithmetic and memory addressing.
Direct-target metadata is relevant only to decoded BRANCH/direct JAL;
do not use the raw B/J interpretation for any other instruction.

Keep the current generic predicted-versus-actual recovery expression,
actual_taken legality/alignment logic, ex_accept gating and all training
rules unchanged. Check target alignment on the captured direct target;
do not truncate it or suppress its low bits. A misaligned taken branch
or jump must still trap, suppress link writes and continue at PC+4.
The captured addresses are exact instruction-derived operands, not
speculative values to be trusted without the existing legality and
direction checks. Wrong directions still recover and squash the
younger instruction before it can store, launch a divide or retire.

This single predictor-datapath hypothesis shares target arithmetic
between early prediction and later recovery instead of recomputing it
in EX. It should preserve all prediction decisions and the baseline's
4,201,709 bracketed CoreMark cycles while reducing EX carry-chain and
routing cost. Added metadata registers and IF fanout are the principal
risks; the worst paths may remain in multiplication or division.
The projected six-percent gain is an unmeasured estimate with low
confidence. The failed local prototypes did not implement this
target-carrying design and are not evidence of its timing or correctness.
Acceptance requires more than 142.69532 iterations/s, approximately
59.956421 MHz if measured cycles remain unchanged.

Preserve nret=1 and every external port, decoder default-illegal
behavior, RVFI order and resolved PC semantics, imem/dmem handshakes,
load-use bubbles, forwarding retention and blocking divider behavior.
Validate unchanged prediction decisions, full-width target arithmetic
including wraparound and alignment, both direction errors, JAL/JALR
links, AUIPC, reset, independently stalled buses and wrong-path side
effects. Run existing unit tests, all unchanged formal/cosimulation
gates, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks and median Gowin
timing. No correctness or timing result is claimed for this final
unimplemented proposal.

title: Prequalify writers and flatten one-hot EX operand selection
motivation:
Recent vendor paths cross forwarding tag comparison, EX operand muxes
and the multiplier. The current EX datapath encodes forwarding choices,
decodes them into a three-way data mux, then selects PC or immediate
through another mux before arithmetic. Prior load-to-branch forwarding
regressed timing, and pipelined multiplication added 4.46 percent more
CoreMark cycles. Shortening existing operand steering offers a local
timing improvement without new bypass paths or execution cycles.

title: Repartition EX timing with registered bypass matches and radix-8 division
motivation:
The champion scores 143.34 iterations/s at 57.009 MHz and 3,977,318
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path crosses 105 cells
inside the divider, from quotient_q to remainder_q. Three dependent
radix-4 subtract/select stages still sit between feedback registers.
Prior structural radix-4 conversion improved fitness at unchanged
latency. The later four-bit launch-peeling attempt regressed after
moving arithmetic into normalization and final acceptance. Blocking
multiplication also paid additional CoreMark cycles. A higher-radix
recurrence can reduce serial depth while keeping all existing register
boundaries and the exact request-to-result schedule. Prototype timing
exposed a second competing path through EX forwarding: radix-8 alone
measured only 53.467 MHz, while early forwarding matches alone measured
53.669 MHz. Applying both parts of the EX timing repartition measured
64.160 MHz. The opportunity is to shorten both competing EX cones
without inserting an instruction stage or paying extra execute cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition EX combinational work at the existing register boundaries:
move forwarding address comparisons before the ID/EX edge and replace
the three-stage divider recurrence with a two-stage radix-8 recurrence.
These are coupled parts of one EX timing redesign; implementing either
alone leaves the competing path dominant in the measured prototypes.
Keep instruction latency, divider latency and the pipeline topology.

In forward_unit add four one-bit registers for rs1/rs2 address matches
against the producer that will occupy EX/MEM or MEM/WB after the next
edge. With stall_id meaning ID/EX holds, compute next_rs1/next_rs2 as
stall_id ? id_ex_rs?_addr : if_id.instr's source bitfields. Compute
next_ex_rd as stall_ex_mem ? ex_mem.rd : id_ex.rd, and next_wb_rd as
hold_mem_wb ? mem_wb.rd : ex_mem.rd. Register each nonzero-source
equality on EVERY non-reset edge, including held ID/EX cycles, and
clear all four flags on reset. Do not freeze match flags just because
the consumer is held: older producers can drain while a divide waits.

After the edge retain live EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write and MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write
qualification of their respective registered match bits, and retain
EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority and the existing 00/01/10 selection encoding.
No five-bit source/destination equality should remain on the EX operand
selection path. Register only address-match metadata, not speculated
reg_write eligibility: actual producer control must still suppress
killed, bubbled or faulting results. In particular keep MEM/WB forwarding
eligible when hold_mem_wb clears retirement valid but retains its data
and control. Do not add valid gating that loses that retained result.
When EX/MEM is cleared during divide wait its reg_write=0 makes a stale
predicted destination harmless. Likewise a flushed consumer's flags
need not match its zeroed source fields because it cannot execute or
retire; compute fresh flags on its next capture. Wire existing hold
signals, queued decode source fields and ID/EX destination into this
unit in core.sv. Leave the hazard and operand-data mux policies intact.

Rebuild the shared DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU recurrence as two serial
radix-8 restoring stages per main iteration, replacing the three
serial radix-4 stages. Retain request capture and signed normalization
on edge 1. On edge 2 retain the existing small first-digit network
that consumes the top TWO dividend bits, and register the full-width
unsigned multiples 3D, 5D, and 7D from the captured normalized divisor.
D, 2D, 4D are widened wires/shifts; 6D is a widened shift of registered
3D. Compute 3D=D+2D, 5D=D+4D, and 7D=8D-D independently in 35 bits,
never in the main feedback cone and never from live EX operands.
The existing first-digit handling for D=0,1,2,3 and D>=4 is unchanged.

Edges 3 through 7 each consume six bits using TWO radix-8 stages.
Thus 2+5*6=32 dividend bits are processed, exactly as before. Each
stage forms the 35-bit trial dividend T={R[31:0],Q[31:29]}. In parallel
compute seven unsigned 36-bit differences {1'b0,T}-{1'b0,kD}, k=1..7.
Difference bit 35 is the borrow. Select the largest fitting multiple
and append its three-bit digit to Q, retaining the selected low 32
remainder bits. With D>0, R<D implies T<8D and the chosen remainder
remains below D, so this truncation is exact. All multiple arithmetic
must preserve 35 bits, including 7D for divisors near 0xffffffff.
Do not implement runtime division/modulo, serial compare-then-subtract,
or a seven-deep priority data mux.

Exploit monotonic fit predicates to keep digit selection shallow:
let fit[k]=!trial[k][35], fit[0]=1, and fit[8]=0. Exactly one
take[k]=fit[k]&&!fit[k+1] is true for k=0..7. Select the remainder
through a balanced eight-way OR of masked candidates (candidate 0
is T); derive the three quotient bits with balanced ORs of the
corresponding take flags. For D=0 every trial fits, so take[7] wins;
the existing captured divide-by-zero override supplies the result.
Use one reused two-stage network, not five unrolled iteration copies.

Preserve edge 8 as the registered CORRECT stage and earliest edge 9
as the EX/MEM result transfer. Preserve the exact state/iteration
schedule under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS with all existing XOR constants.
The EX handshake, saved forwarded RVFI operands, stable held result,
reset cancellation, signed truncation, remainder sign, division by
zero and INT_MIN/-1 behavior stay intact. Keep nret=1, decoder legality,
memory backpressure, retirement order, multiplier, predictor and the
four-entry fetch queue unchanged. Do not weaken any test or formal
bound, and do not change evaluation or contract files.

Fourteen parallel trial subtractors replace nine, but only two digit
selections are serial instead of three, while forwarding comparisons
terminate at four new metadata registers before EX. Target a 12 percent
net fitness improvement with medium confidence. Subtractor area, divisor
fanout, wider selection and a newly dominant EX path may limit the
benefit. Validate real arithmetic and ALTOPS tests, unchanged formal
and stalled cosimulation, and canonical
CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks. Inspect vendor critical paths
and measure all three Gowin placement options and actual cycles.
Acceptance requires fitness above 149.93364 iterations/s; if cycles
remain 3,977,318, median Fmax must exceed 59.63338 MHz.

A disposable prototype of both changes measured Gowin placement options
0/1/2 at 63.426/64.160/64.160 MHz, median 64.160 MHz. Option 0 used
4,482 logic cells, 885 FFs, 49 LUT-RAM, four BSRAM and six DSPs. Its
leading paths were WB selection through EX arithmetic and the shortened
divider recurrence, approximately 21.06 ns arrival. The combined design
completed canonical stalled CoreMark in exactly 3,977,318 bracketed
cycles, passing all CRC/UART/bounds/completion/marker validation. This
projects 161.3147 iterations/s, 12.54 percent above 143.34. All existing
ALU tests plus an added radix-8 boundary test passed in real and ALTOPS
builds (31 tests each), retaining exact latency checks; both pipeline
test variants passed all 27 tests. Reference cosimulation passed
selftest plus three random programs with and without stalls. All 53
unchanged ALTOPS formal checks passed, including reg_ch0, pc_fwd,
liveness and unique; lint also passed. ALTOPS does not prove the real
radix-8 arithmetic, which the real-arithmetic vectors exercise.
These are prototype results, not
orchestrator acceptance. Reproduce unchanged correctness and median
vendor timing gates after implementation; do not substitute a faster
placement option for the median or omit CoreMark cycle measurement.

title: Verify predicted conditional branches in MEM to absorb load-use bubbles
motivation:
The current 64-entry bimodal predictor and four-entry fetch queue already
remove most direct-control bubbles. Prior profiling found approximately
52,000 conditional misses, making accuracy expansion alone insufficient
for the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold. Local table-storage, smaller
predictor and static-prediction probes also failed to improve fitness;
the unchanged parent reproduced 57.009 MHz and 3,977,318 CoreMark cycles.

A more useful predictor integration is to let predicted branches proceed
while their load operands are still being produced, then verify them one
stage later. LESSONS.md records that r7s0 removed 3.26 percent of cycles
with branch-only MEM-to-EX load forwarding but lost fitness on timing.
Delayed verification can remove those load-use bubbles using registered
WB data, avoiding that failed same-cycle memory-to-EX comparator path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move verification and training of all legal conditional BRANCH instructions
from EX to MEM, retaining the existing IF bimodal prediction policy and
instruction queue. This is one predictor-integration change: predict in
IF, carry the prediction, and verify conditional outcomes in MEM. Direct
JAL and JALR continue resolving in EX, subject to older MEM-branch recovery.
Do not add a predictor table, cache, return stack, or arithmetic redesign.

Remove the load-use bubble only when the presented valid decode head is
a positively recognized legal conditional branch. Preserve load-use
interlocks for every other instruction, including reserved branch funct3
values. The branch may enter EX immediately behind its producing load.
If that older load stalls in MEM, existing data backpressure still holds
the branch and both stages until the load is accepted. This optimization
never bypasses the bus handshake or consumes unready load data.

EX prepares the full direct branch target, PC, decoded condition type,
original predicted_taken, source register numbers and operand values for
MEM verification. Reuse ex_mem_t's existing branch_target, PC and source
fields; add only the prediction bit and two deferred-load operand flags.
For each source matched by the valid immediately older EX/MEM load's
nonzero rd, mark that operand for repair from the next cycle's WB result.
Do not capture that load's EX/MEM alu_result as an operand: it is its
address, not loaded data. All other branch operands use ordinary EX
forwarding and are captured on the branch's actual EX acceptance edge.

Preserve a correct fallback value for each deferred operand. Compute it
from the normal captured register value and any matching retained MEM/WB
forwarding value, excluding the pending EX/MEM load. In MEM, substitute
wb_w_data only if that immediately older load actually writes the matching
nonzero register; otherwise use the fallback. This matters when a
misaligned load traps and suppresses its write. Do not treat mem_read or
matching rd alone as proof of a valid load result. During a data stall,
retain the existing WB forwarding data so the eventual fallback capture
remains correct. Both source operands may depend on the same load.

MEM resolves all six branch conditions from these captured/repaired
operands, uses the registered full branch target, checks taken-target
alignment, and derives the architectural next PC. Train the existing
current-entry two-bit counter once when this valid legal branch advances
to WB, excluding faulting taken branches. A not-taken branch with an
unaligned encoded target remains legal and trains not taken. No branch
training occurs in EX. Update RVFI source values, resolved pc_next and
trap controls from this same verified outcome; prediction is never an
architectural result. Preserve existing fallthrough behavior on faults.

A MEM conditional misprediction has priority over any younger EX jump,
instruction-bus availability, queue activity and younger execution wait.
On correction, retire the resolving older branch normally, discard the
entire fetch queue, flush ID/EX, and inject a completely cleared EX/MEM
bubble instead of accepting the younger EX instruction. Suppress that
younger instruction's redirect and divider request on the correction
cycle. Gate EX acceptance/divider launch and arrange hold-versus-flush
priority explicitly: an execute_wait signal from a wrong-path divide
must not block the older branch's correction. A valid branch in MEM has
no data-memory transaction, so its resolution is not held by unrelated
io_dmemReady. Preserve normal downstream holds when no MEM correction is
present. Correct predictions allow the younger EX instruction to proceed.

Keep EX JAL/JALR legality, alignment, link values and target calculations
unchanged. Merge their redirect with MEM correction by instruction age.
A wrong-path store must never enter EX/MEM, and a wrong-path divide must
never launch. Preserve full-width addresses, decoder default-illegal
behavior, every nret=1 top-level port, precise single retirement and +1
order, retained forwarding, arithmetic/ALTOPS and memory-side handshakes.
Do not alter any correctness gate, benchmark, wrapper or timing contract.

The tradeoff is one extra recovery cycle per conditional misprediction
versus removal of load-to-branch interlocks and relocation of the branch
comparator/recovery logic away from EX. The prior 3.26 percent saving
and approximately 52,000 misses suggest a net cycle opportunity near
two percent, but those measurements precede this exact integration and
are not a prediction of its measured cycles. Clearing the acceptance
threshold therefore also needs a modest frequency improvement. Estimate
six percent net gain with low confidence. Added timed operand registers,
WB-to-MEM repair muxes and the still-critical divider are material risks.
No implementation or timing result is claimed for this final proposal;
the rejected local predictor-storage probes did not implement it.

Validate the saved bubble on repeated correctly predicted load-dependent
branches with every branch condition and either/both matching sources.
Test prolonged independent bus stalls, prior WB writers, misaligned
trapping loads, both correction directions, full-queue recovery and
target misalignment. Place JALR, load, store, illegal instructions and
DIV/REM immediately behind a mispredicted branch; check that MEM recovery
wins without a wrong-path request, register write, training or retirement.
Check exact RVFI operands, next PCs, trap flags and contiguous order.
Update predictor timing observations for MEM training and the additional
recovery stage while preserving every architectural assertion. Run the
existing unit, unchanged formal and stalled reference-cosimulation gates,
then canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation and all three
Gowin placement options. Accept only above 149.93364 iterations/s.

title: Remove avoidable control muxes from the registered WB-to-EX result loop
motivation:
The champion scores 153.70 iterations/s at 61.131 MHz and 3,977,318
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at MEM/WB.mem_to_reg
and ends at EX/MEM.alu_result through WB selection, forwarding and
arithmetic. The loop contains a load/ALU selector after the launch
register and an invalid-bubble zero selector before the destination
register. Neither selector needs to occupy that timed arithmetic path.
Registered forwarding address matches are already present. Prior
one-hot operand selection alone regressed; this proposal moves or
removes result-data selection at existing register boundaries.

using the existing aligned, sign/zero-extended load_data. In wb_stage
drive w_data directly from in.wb_data, retaining w_en and w_addr exactly.

a WB load/ALU mux. Preserve EX/MEM.alu_result and effective_addr, and
all raw RVFI memory fields; raw mem_rdata is not the extended load value.
Reset clears wb_data. hold_wb retains it with destination and controls
while clearing only valid, preserving post-retirement WB forwarding.
Do not introduce valid or reg_write gating on this payload capture.

Second remove the bubble-zero selector at the arithmetic-result
register's input. Change only EX/MEM.alu_result's behavior on the
existing execute_wait or !in.valid bubble arm in ex_stage. Retain
reset-first and data-memory-stall-second priority. On reset clear the
entire bundle; on stall retain it completely. On an unstalled bubble

same candidate captured for a real instruction:
  in.ctrl.is_jump ? (in.pc + 32'd4) : alu_result.

in the same bubble arm and the same existing always_ff process. The
later field assignment overrides the bundle zero. Keep the normal
valid-instruction arm unchanged. Equivalently, the result register

title: Capture multiply operands and use EX/MEM as the product register
motivation:
The champion scores 153.70 iterations/s at 61.131 MHz with 3,977,318
CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path runs from WB selection through
EX forwarding and the ALU into EX/MEM.alu_result. The prior r5s1
structural multiplier improved frequency but inserted two wait cycles
per multiply, increasing CoreMark cycles by 4.46 percent. A multiplier
operand boundary can remove forwarding from the arithmetic path while
using the existing EX/MEM register to avoid that extra completion cycle.

hypothesis.motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the three combinational multiply expressions with one shared
signed 33-by-33 multiplier fed exclusively by captured operands. Use
a two-cycle blocking EX transaction: edge 1 captures the exact forwarded
operands and multiply opcode; edge 2 captures the selected product
directly in the existing EX/MEM.alu_result register and releases EX.
There is exactly ONE added wait cycle per multiply when MEM is ready.
Do not add a separate multiplier-result register or a third transfer
edge. Base ALU operations retain their existing latency and divider
arithmetic, latency and handshake remain unchanged.

In alu.sv add mul_req_valid/mul_req_ready and
mul_result_valid/mul_result_ready. A pending bit is zero when idle.
On request acceptance save 32-bit A, B and the opcode, and set pending.
While pending assert result_valid, deassert req_ready and keep operands
unchanged; clear pending only on result transfer or reset. The result
is combinational from these saved operands and stays stable under
backpressure. A's signed extension bit is saved A[31] only for MULH
and MULHSU; B's is saved B[31] only for MULH. Otherwise extend with
zero. Multiply explicit signed 33-bit operands into a signed 66-bit
product. Select bits 31:0 for MUL and bits 63:32 for MULH/MULHU/MULHSU.
Bits 65:64 are not part of the architectural high result. Remove the
old live-input products so forwarding terminates at the operand
registers instead of feeding the product logic on the same cycle.
Sign extension and high/low result
selection use the captured opcode, not the live instruction.

In EX recognize only the four multiply operations. Launch once for
a valid multiply when !stall and mul_req_ready. Assert execute_wait
for a valid multiply without result_valid, OR the existing divide
wait. Set result_ready only for the held valid multiply with !stall.
The existing hazard logic holds ID/EX and decode consumption while
older MEM/WB work drains and fetch can fill its queue. A dmem stall
keeps priority: preserve its EX/MEM request, then accept the multiply
only when that older transaction can advance. During the launch wait,
emit a fully cleared EX/MEM bubble rather than clearing valid alone.
On the following available edge, normal EX/MEM capture registers the
product and accepts the held decode successor. That successor receives
the product through ordinary EX/MEM or MEM/WB forwarding.

Save the original post-forwarding source values at multiply launch
for RVFI, sharing the existing divide operand-history registers since
blocking EX allows only one such operation at a time. Use saved values
at multiply retirement even if live forwarding producers have drained.
Keep multiply and divide transaction state independent; consecutive
multiplies and alternating MUL/DIV must neither relaunch nor consume
stale completion. Reset clears pending work. Wrong-path or invalid
instructions must not launch, retire or cause a memory side effect.
Preserve held MEM/WB forwarding, younger-writer priority, x0 behavior,
load-use bubbles, legality/traps, branch recovery and nret=1 IO.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS retain the SAME request edge, pending cycle
and earliest edge-2 transfer. Compute the existing MUL/MULH/MULHU
add-XOR and MULHSU subtract-XOR formulas from saved operands and opcode,
using the original constants. Only arithmetic changes under ALTOPS;
no formal-only latency shortcut is allowed. No change to wrappers,
formal bounds, benchmarks, memory contracts or correctness gates.

title: Persistent bimodal predictor with registered EX training
motivation:
The champion already predicts direct BRANCH/JAL and buffers four fetches.
Prior profiling found only about 52,000 conditional misses; fresh trace
replay counts just 13,735 returns, so larger direction tables and return
prediction have limited cycle headroom. LESSONS.md records clock gains
from removing predictor reset logic on older parents, but carrying direct
targets regressed and MEM-stage verification failed liveness.

On this exact parent, placement-option-1 probes measured 59.318 MHz for
persistent counters alone and 61.346 MHz for registered training alone.
Combining persistent counters with registered training measured 64.119 MHz
in the same vendor flow. The former exposes WB/EX-to-counter training as
a worst path; registering that event isolates counter updates while the
persistent bank removes reset-related logic. This is one predictor
implementation change with complementary parts, not an accuracy redesign.

a held EX instruction cannot duplicate training. Back-to-back branches
can supply one event per cycle while the prior event drains. Read the
current table entry at update time, not a saved lookup counter, so two
consecutive outcomes for the same entry accumulate without lost updates.
Fetch observes pre-edge counter state; the one-cycle later update can
change prediction timing, but EX always verifies the captured prediction.
Never flush an older pending training event on a younger recovery.

Retain all 64 counters, binary encoding, PC[7:2] indexing, saturation and
prediction policies. Initialize counters[i] to weakly taken 2'b10 in a
synthesizable initial loop, using the same initialization in Gowin,
simulation and formal. Remove only the bank's synchronous reset arm;
its existing indexed saturating update is enabled by

PC, pipeline, register file, divider and RVFI order exactly as before;
only advisory predictor history survives. Discard any pending training
event when reset is asserted. No epoch, clearing sweep or startup stall
is needed; correctness must hold for arbitrary retained history.

misalignment handling, EX redirect and recovery stay on their existing
cycle. Preserve the one-bit prediction packet, four-entry fetch queue,
empty bypass, queue flush priority, load-use interlocks, bus handshakes,
forwarding, divider/ALTOPS, decoder legality, full addresses and nret=1.
Do not add target prediction, late verification, a new execution stage
or any other category change.

The goal is to terminate EX's outcome/qualification fanout at a small
register bank and let counter lookup, saturation and write selection
operate from registered inputs. Reset removal alone exposes a path from
WB write qualification through EX to the counter bank. In the combined
prototype the worst vendor path returns to the divider, with competing
WB-to-ALU paths. The predictor was not the champion's recorded worst
path; attribute the gain to training isolation plus physical changes,
not a change to arithmetic depth or prediction accuracy.

An isolated prototype of exactly this two-part predictor change measured
Gowin placement-option Fmax values of 61.846, 64.119 and 64.119 MHz:

RAM conversion; preserve the existing array and indexed saturation form.
The benchmark completed with unchanged 3,977,318 marker-bracketed cycles,

This implies 161.21165 iterations/s, 4.887 percent above 153.70, exceeding
the 160.7702 acceptance threshold by only 0.44145 iterations/s. Round the
expected gain to five percent with medium confidence. Final implementation
must reproduce the vendor median; the margin is small.

The prototype passed reference cosimulation of selftest and all three
random programs, each with and without independent bus stalls. A directed
cocotb probe passed 26 executions across runtime resets, observing exact
pre-edge predictions and pending event fields against a retained abstract
counter model. It observed 34 accepted training events, 33 applications
and one deliberately reset-canceled event; it checked aliased outcomes,

order and precise PC traces. All 53 unchanged standard ALTOPS formal
checks passed, including liveness and register consistency. These are

Adapt the full existing pipeline predictor observer to model the delayed

entry-local update logic, RAM attributes, resizing or speculative state.

title: Replace radix-8 adjacent-fit masking with balanced monotonic-fit selection
motivation: The champion scores 161.21 iterations/s at 64.119 MHz and its reported worst path crosses two radix-8 subtract/select stages. Prior byte carry-select logic regressed. On this parent, grouped-prefix, enlarged-preparation, narrowed-trial and radix-64 probes also failed to improve timing. Direct balanced selection preserves the small native subtractors and is the strongest observed isolated divider change: a two-stage selector prototype measured 64.342 MHz for placement option 1, with the leading paths moving to WB/EX and branch recovery. That probe does not clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.

On this parent, grouped-prefix, enlarged-preparation, narrowed-trial and radix-64 probes also failed to improve timing. Direct balanced selection preserves the small native subtractors and is the strongest observed isolated divider change: a two-stage selector prototype measured 64.342 MHz for placement option 1, with the leading paths moving to WB/EX and branch recovery. That probe does not clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the remainder and quotient digit selection in the current radix-8 divider with balanced selection driven directly by monotonic fit predicates. Keep all seven full-width native subtractions in each stage, the original registered 35-bit divisor multiples, and the original two-bit preparation peel. Do not use the regressing narrowed-arithmetic, carry-prefix or radix-64 variants.

In each stage fit[k]=!trial[k][35], for k=1..7. Select trial 6 or 7 with fit[7], trial 4 or 5 with fit[5], and select those pairs with fit[6]. Similarly select trial 2 or 3 with fit[3], shifted or trial 1 with fit[1], and select those pairs with fit[2]. Finally select the upper or lower half with fit[4]. All candidates use their low 32 bits. This is a balanced three-level mux tree whose control fits are computed in parallel, not a seven-deep priority chain. Derive quotient bit 2 as fit[4], bit 1 as fit[4]?fit[6]:fit[2], and bit 0 as fit[4]?(fit[6]?fit[7]:fit[5]):(fit[2]?fit[3]:fit[1]). The ordered multiples make the fit vector monotonic; the tree therefore chooses exactly the largest fitting digit. D=0 makes all fits true and chooses digit seven, with the unchanged final zero-divisor override providing the architectural answer.

The intent is to remove adjacent-fit take[k] generation, candidate masking and eight-way OR reduction from the dependent remainder path, allowing the FPGA mapper to use direct hierarchical muxes. This is one local arithmetic-selector micro-optimization. Preserve 2+5*6=32 consumed bits and every state/handshake: edge 1 captures/normalizes, edge 2 peels two bits and registers odd multiples, edges 3..7 iterate, edge 8 corrects and asserts result_valid, and edge 9 is the earliest consumption. Preserve ALTOPS arithmetic and schedule, signed and unsigned corner cases, reset cancellation and held completion. Leave all other RTL, nret=1, decoder legality, memory, forwarding, prediction and verification contracts unchanged.

The placement-option-1 prototype used 4,053 logic cells, 893 FFs, 49 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs, at 64.342 MHz. This is approximately 0.35 percent frequency improvement, not an accepted candidate and not a three-option median. The expected gain is conservatively rounded to one percent with low confidence, below the acceptance threshold. A gain above 4.6 percent is not supported by this probe; competing EX paths and placement sensitivity are the major risks. The implementer must retain the single selector focus and measure the complete normal vendor median before claiming a gain. Acceptance requires more than 168.62566 iterations/s, approximately 67.069 MHz at unchanged 3,977,318 bracketed cycles.

Validate selection equivalence for all eight monotonic patterns of seven fit bits and arbitrary candidate data. Run real and ALTOPS ALU vectors with unchanged latency checks, existing pipeline/formal and stalled reference cosimulation, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks, and all normal Gowin placement options. ALTOPS alone cannot prove real arithmetic. Do not weaken any gate or formal depth and do not claim acceptance from a best placement result.

title: Repartition M-extension execution at operand and completion registers
motivation:
The champion scores 161.21 iterations/s at 64.119 MHz and 3,977,318
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path crosses 76 cells
inside the divider, from quotient_q to remainder_q. The current main
recurrence performs two dependent radix-8 subtract/select stages per
clock. Prior structural attempts show that shortening divider feedback
can improve the global clock, but extra divide cycles threaten the
unchanged formal liveness bound. The r6s1 launch-peeling experiment
also warns against moving multiple generation onto forwarded inputs.
The r9s1 multiplier experiment exposed this same divider bottleneck.
A new divider-only prototype measured 64.578 MHz median with unchanged
cycles, exposing WB forwarding through the multiplier as the worst
path. Either change alone leaves the competing M-extension path
dominant. Address both with one execution-register partitioning change.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition the M-extension execution unit at its operand and completion
register boundaries: capture forwarded multiply operands before the
product, and shorten divider feedback to one radix-32 digit per clock.
These complementary parts address the competing paths measured in the
divider-only probe and the prior multiplier-only attempt; this is one
structural execution timing redesign, with no predictor or memory change.

For MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU add a separate request/result handshake in
alu.sv. On accepted request edge 1 capture the original 32-bit operands
and opcode and set a pending bit. While pending, hold them unchanged,
deassert request-ready and assert result-valid. Build one signed
33-by-33 product with a full 66-bit result from these saved operands.
Extend A with its sign only for MULH/MULHSU and B only for MULH;
otherwise extend with zero. Select product[31:0] for saved MUL or
product[63:32] for saved high-product operations. Do not truncate the
operands or use the live opcode for product signedness or selection.
The existing EX/MEM register captures the product on the next available
edge, earliest edge 2. Do not add another product/result register or
another wait cycle. Remove all old live-input multiplication expressions.
Pending clears only on accepted completion or reset; result remains
stable under backpressure. Keep saved 32-bit operands plus opcode,
rather than registering already sign-extended operands: the latter
mapped worse in the prior r9s1 probe.

Extend EX execute_wait for an incomplete multiply, preserving the
existing divide wait and dmem priority. Launch once only for a valid
multiply when an older memory transaction can advance; preserve full
EX/MEM bubbles while waiting and let older instructions drain. Save
original forwarded rs1/rs2 on multiply launch in the existing divide
RVFI operand registers, since blocking EX permits only one active
operation. Transfer once, then let ordinary EX/MEM forwarding supply
the immediate consumer. Keep multiply/divide pending state distinct;
consecutive MUL and alternating MUL/DIV must not reuse stale results.
Under ALTOPS compute the existing four multiply XOR formulas from
captured operands/opcode with the identical edge-2 transfer schedule.

Repartition the shared blocking divider around a single radix-32
restoring digit per iteration. Keep signed operand capture at request
edge 1 and the existing two-bit prefix peel at edge 2. At edge 2 also
register all nontrivial odd multiples of the captured unsigned divisor.
Run six five-bit digit iterations on edges 3 through 8, consuming
exactly 2 + 6*5 = 32 dividend bits. Remove the dedicated CORRECT cycle
and corrected-result register: while DONE, form sign correction and
exceptional-result selection from the stable final state registers,
letting the existing EX/MEM register capture the architectural result
on edge 9 at the earliest. Its external request/completion interface
and complete divide latency remain unchanged. Multiplication adds
exactly one EX wait cycle; do not add a formal-only shortcut.

Preserve the current small prefix network for D=0,1,2,3 and D>=4.
At request capture normalized 32-bit A and D, original dividend and
sign/operation/exception metadata exactly as today. Do not compute
wide multiples or the prefix before this normalization register.
At the preparation edge register 37-bit 3D,5D,...,31D using explicit
widened shifts and short add/sub expressions from registered D.
For reproducibility use canonical signed-digit forms: 3=4-1, 5=4+1,
7=8-1, 9=8+1, 11=16-4-1, 13=16-4+1, 15=16-1, 17=16+1,
19=16+4-1, 21=16+4+1, 23=32-8-1, 25=32-8+1, 27=32-4-1,
29=32-4+1, and 31=32-1, each term denoting a widened shift of D.
D and powers of two are wiring; other even multiples are shifts of
the corresponding registered odd multiple. Preserve all high bits:
31*(2^32-1) fits in 37 bits. Do not serially generate each multiple
from its predecessor or place multiple generation in the feedback
path. Use shift/add/sub expressions rather than general multipliers.

Each reused main iteration forms the 37-bit unsigned trial dividend
T={remainder_q[31:0],quotient_q[31:27]}. Compute the 31 differences
{1'b0,T}-{1'b0,kD}, k=1..31, in parallel at 38-bit width; bit 37
indicates borrow. Define fit[0]=1, fit[32]=0 and
fit[k]=!trial[k][37]. Select digit k with
take[k]=fit[k] && !fit[k+1]. For nonzero D the fits are monotonic;
R<D implies T<32D, and the selected remainder is again below D.
Select its low 32 bits through an explicitly balanced 32-way masked
OR tree, with candidate zero equal to T. Form each quotient-digit
bit from a balanced OR of the appropriate one-hot take bits, then
shift quotient_q by five and append that digit. Avoid priority mux
ladders and separate compare-then-subtract chains. For D=0 all trials
fit and digit 31 is deterministic; the saved exception flag supplies
the architectural result. Keep only one reused digit network.

Preparation is iteration index 0; indices 1 through 6 perform the
six full digits, entering DONE after index 6. In DONE result_valid
is asserted and req_ready is low. Combinational result selects the
final quotient or remainder, restores the captured sign and applies
division-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 overrides. It must depend only on
held registers, never live operands or combinational next-iteration
values. Hold all state and result stable until result_ready; reset
cancels pending work. Keep IDLE=0, ITERATE=1 and DONE=3; CORRECT need
not remain a functional state. Preserve truncation toward zero and
the dividend's sign on a nonzero remainder.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS retain original captured operands/opcode,
the identical preparation plus six-iteration schedule, and the exact
existing DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU XOR formulas as the held combinational
completion value. Earliest transfer remains edge 9 in both builds.
Preserve EX's saved RVFI operands, once-only launch/transfer, full
EX/MEM wait bubbles, older MEM/WB draining and data-stall priority.
Keep nret=1, top-level ports, decoder legality, traps, memory protocol,
forwarding priority, prediction and retirement order unchanged.
No contract files, formal bounds or architectural checks may change.

Expect a 6 percent fitness gain with medium confidence, supported by
the combined prototype below. A single carry/select stage replaces
two in divider feedback without adding divide cycles;
multiplier operand registers remove forwarding from the product path.
The main risks are the larger 31-candidate network, multiple-register
fanout and routing, preparation arithmetic, the registered product
path and extra multiply wait cycles. Correction ends at EX/MEM rather
than an internal divider register and must be checked as a potential
new timing limit.

A disposable combined prototype measured Gowin placement options
0/1/2 at 64.159/68.485/68.485 MHz, for a median of 68.485 MHz.
Placement 0 used 5,765 logic cells, 1,356 FFs, 49 LUT-RAMs, four
BSRAMs and two DSPs. CoreMark passed the canonical CRC/UART/bounds/
completion/marker validator at 3,989,539 bracketed cycles, only
0.31 percent more than the champion. The product is 171.66144
iterations/s, a 6.483 percent gain over 161.21. This exceeds the
168.62566 acceptance threshold, but is prototype evidence rather than
final orchestrator acceptance. Reproduce all three vendor placements.
The leading combined-prototype paths now run from held MEM/WB write
qualification through EX toward fetch/decode, with ordinary EX result
logic also competitive; divider feedback no longer leads the reports.
Do not add another optimization to these newly exposed paths here.

The combined prototype passed lint, all 31 existing pipeline tests in
each of the normal and YOSYS-declaration builds, and 32 ALU tests in
each of the real and ALTOPS builds. ALU tests retained all arithmetic
references and exact divide-latency assertions, adapted multiply to
captured operands and held completion, and added radix-32 boundary
cases plus 768 random operand pairs for all four division operations.
Stalled selftest reference cosimulation also passed. All 53 unchanged
ALTOPS formal checks passed, including liveness, PC continuity,
register consistency and unique retirement order. Final implementation
must rerun every gate. ALTOPS does not prove the real arithmetic.

Validate the existing real and ALTOPS ALU suites, including exact
latency and held-completion assertions, plus pipeline tests, unchanged
formal and stalled reference cosimulation. Add radix-32 boundary
vectors and retain all existing arithmetic and handshake coverage.
Run canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation and median
Gowin timing for all placement options. Acceptance requires fitness
greater than 168.62566 iterations/s. The previous one-wait-cycle
multiplier probe used 3,989,539 cycles; at that cycle count median
Fmax must exceed approximately 67.274 MHz. Confirm both the
cycle count and disappearance of the two-stage divider feedback path.

title: Selectively verify load-dependent predicted branches in MEM
motivation:
The existing predictor and fetch queue already remove most direct-control bubbles. Prior profiling reports roughly 52,000 conditional misses and 13,735 returns, so improving accuracy alone offers little headroom. Current-parent probes of counter rewrites and split lookup/training storage reduced area in some cases but did not establish the required clock gain. The remaining promising predictor angle is hiding branch operand latency.

LESSONS.md records a 3.26 percent cycle saving from eliminating load-to-branch interlocks, but direct memory-to-EX forwarding lost Fmax. The r8s2 proposal moved every conditional branch's verification to MEM and failed the unchanged liveness check. Selective verification can target the load-use bubbles without imposing that extra recovery cycle on independent branches.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the existing 64-entry persistent bimodal predictor, registered training stage and four-entry fetch queue. Remove the load-use interlock only for a positively decoded legal conditional branch whose source depends on the immediately preceding valid load's nonzero destination. Issue this branch using its captured prediction, defer its operand verification to MEM, and obtain the load result from the existing registered WB path. All other conditional branches and all JAL/JALR continue resolving in EX. This is one predictor integration change, not a new direction algorithm or arithmetic redesign.

Identify the exceptional branch in EX by matching either source against the immediately older EX/MEM load, with valid, mem_read and rd!=0 qualification. Carry a deferred-branch bit, two operand-repair flags and the original prediction in EX/MEM. Reuse its existing full-width branch_target, PC, source addresses and source values. A branch immediately behind a load may advance early only because this deferred path will verify it; ordinary load-use interlocks remain for all nonbranches and reserved branch encodings. Data-bus backpressure still holds the load and following branch until the load is accepted.

For each matched operand, retain the value that would exist if the older load does not write: prefer a matching retained MEM/WB writer, otherwise use the captured ID/EX value. Exclude the pending EX/MEM load's alu_result, which is its address, from this fallback. In MEM, replace only marked operands with WB data when the immediately older load actually writes that matching nonzero destination. A trapping misaligned load suppresses its write, so the fallback is required. Repair both sources independently, including the case where both read the same destination. Unmatched operands keep normal forwarded EX values.

For a deferred branch only, suppress EX condition-based redirect, training and target-fault decisions. In MEM compute the six architectural branch conditions from the repaired operands, check the registered target's alignment and resolve pc_next and traps exactly as the original EX path did. Report the repaired source values through RVFI. A not-taken branch with an unaligned encoded target remains legal; an actually taken misaligned branch traps and continues at PC+4. Nondeferred instructions keep the existing MEM behavior.

A deferred MEM misprediction takes priority over every younger EX action. Retire the older branch normally, redirect IF, discard the complete fetch queue, flush ID/EX, and clear EX/MEM instead of capturing the younger instruction. Suppress younger divider requests, EX redirects and training on that edge. Recovery must beat a wrong-path divide's execute_wait; arrange kill priority explicitly before hold/accept decisions. The resolving MEM branch has no data-memory operation, so unrelated io_dmemReady cannot stall it. Correctly predicted deferred branches permit the younger instruction to advance normally. Preserve immediate EX recovery for all ordinary branches and jumps.

MEM and EX can both offer branch training on a correctly predicted deferred branch followed by another conditional branch. Define a simple, explicit arbitration policy: the accepted legal nonfaulting MEM event has priority; if an accepted EX event coincides, discard only that younger learning event. A squashed EX branch never trains. This advisory drop changes prediction quality only and avoids adding a two-write table, training queue or execution stall. Train all noncolliding accepted eligible branches once, retaining the current one-cycle registered training stage and live-entry saturation. Test the intentional collision behavior rather than assuming every accepted branch always trains.

This selective exception addresses the earlier liveness failure structurally. In a zero-wait load/branch pair, the new branch verifies in MEM on the same edge where the original interlocked branch would have verified in EX. A correct prediction saves the bubble; a misprediction does not acquire the extra recovery cycle imposed by moving every branch to MEM. Independent conditional branches keep their original recovery timing. This timing argument is not a proof: unchanged liveness, register-consistency, instruction, trap and uniqueness checks must all pass without changing formal depth or assumptions.

The prior 3.26 percent cycle saving is evidence of available load-branch bubbles on an older parent, not a measured result for this proposal. Estimate six percent net fitness improvement with low confidence: roughly three percent fewer cycles plus an unproven modest physical timing gain. Keeping data-memory output out of EX avoids the specific path that hurt r7s0; it does not itself establish a frequency improvement over this interlocked champion. At the historical 3.26 percent cycle saving, passing the current 168.62566 iterations/s threshold needs approximately 64.88 MHz, versus the champion's 64.119 MHz. Added repair muxes, recovery fanout, learning collisions and the still-critical divider may prevent this gain. No implementation, correctness or timing result is claimed for this selective design.

Check cycle savings on warm correctly predicted load-branch loops and unchanged independent-branch recovery latency. Run the existing unit suite, unchanged formal and stalled reference cosimulation, then canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation and median Gowin timing.

The r9s0 result-loop optimization was limited by the old radix-8 divider; the champion has since removed that competing limit with radix-32 division and captured multiply operands. Optimize both ends of this same register-to-register result path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Optimize the data/control partition at both ends of the existing registered WB-to-EX result loop. Move the load-versus-ALU writeback selection before MEM/WB, and remove bubble-zero selection from the receiving EX/MEM arithmetic payload. This is one local result-loop micro-optimization, adding no instruction stage or cycles.

Replace only mem_wb_t.alu_result and mem_wb_t.read_data with a single 32-bit wb_data. On each ordinary MEM/WB advance capture:
  reg_q.wb_data <= in.ctrl.mem_to_reg ? load_data : in.alu_result;
Use the existing byte/halfword sign- or zero-extended load_data, not raw dmem_rdata. In wb_stage drive w_data directly from in.wb_data. Keep w_en=in.ctrl.reg_write&&in.valid and w_addr=in.rd exactly.

Reset clears wb_data. A data-memory hold retains wb_data together with destination and control fields while clearing only valid, exactly as today. Retained WB data remains a forwarding source after retirement-valid clears. Capture the selected payload on every existing non-held advance without adding valid, reg_write or exception gating. Preserve EX/MEM.alu_result and effective_addr, raw RVFI memory data, trap-adjusted controls, all load widths/signs, x0 and youngest-writer priority. Leave unrelated bundle controls alone and update obsolete payload comments.

At the receiving end change only EX/MEM.alu_result's bubble behavior. Keep reset-first and data-memory-hold-second priority. Reset clears the full bundle; a data stall retains all of it. In the existing execute_wait-or-invalid bubble arm keep reg_q <= '0 and then override this single field:
  reg_q.alu_result <= in.ctrl.is_jump ? (in.pc + 32'd4) : alu_result;
The later field assignment must override the bundle clear in the same always_ff process. Keep the normal valid capture arm unchanged. The unused result payload now captures on every unstalled, non-reset edge; all other bubble bits remain zero. Do not replace the zero mux with a bubble-dependent hold enable, which would preserve the late control dependency.

Every bubble must still clear valid, reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, destination and all other metadata. Forwarding inspects reg_write independently of valid, so clearing only valid is insufficient. The unused payload must never cause a register write, memory request, predictor update or retirement. Preserve reset and stall priorities, M-extension request/completion schedules, RVFI source/result values and once-only retirement. Do not add comparator, predictor, bypass-policy or arithmetic-unit changes. Keep nret=1, top-level IO, decoder legality, real/ALTOPS arithmetic and all verification contracts unchanged.

Adapt the representation-specific complete-bubble-equals-zero assertion in multiply_radix32_forwarding_and_transaction_order to check the exact new bundle value. At each unstalled M-wait edge record the ALU candidate; on the next observation require the entire EX/MEM bundle to equal that candidate in alu_result and zero in every other bit. EX/MEM packs pc then alu_result, so the candidate shift is bundle_width-64. M-wait instructions cannot be jumps. Do not simply ignore the payload or remove the assertion. Keep all architectural, memory, source-value, prediction, launch/transfer timing, retirement and trace checks. This preserves an exact-state check and every architectural bubble guarantee.

The mapped circuit launches from a final WB-data register without a load/ALU output mux and captures the EX result without bubble-zero selection. The redundant WB payload bank disappears. WB-selection-only testing on this champion reached 77.044 MHz median, about four percent gain, insufficient for acceptance; the final proposal optimizes both endpoints of the same result loop. Final implementation must pass every unchanged gate, including register consistency, PC continuity, liveness and unique retirement. Do not alter formal depths or contract files. Add directed mixed-width loads, ALU/M-extension/link values and immediate consumers, same-rd writers, x0, misalignment, reset and prolonged dmem holds that retain WB forwarding after valid clears. title: Retiming writeback selection into a single MEM/WB result register
motivation:
The champion scores 185.62 iterations/s at 74.054 MHz and 3,989,539
bracketed CoreMark cycles. After r10s1 shortened competing M-extension
paths, its worst reported path starts at MEM/WB read_data, crosses WB
and EX, and ends at the fetch PC. The current MEM/WB boundary registers
ALU and extended load data separately, then selects between them in WB.
That late wide mux feeds forwarding, branch/JALR recovery and the
register-file write bypass. Structural r8s1 showed that moving work
across existing boundaries can help without adding instruction cycles;
r8s0 also showed that a combinational mux rewrite alone is insufficient.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move architectural writeback-data selection across the existing MEM/WB
clock boundary. Replace mem_wb_t's separately registered alu_result and
read_data with one 32-bit result field. In mem_stage calculate the same
sign/zero-extended load_data as today, then capture
in.ctrl.mem_to_reg ? load_data : in.alu_result into result on every
normal MEM/WB advance edge. wb_stage wires w_data directly to result,
retaining its existing valid/reg_write write enable and destination.
This is one structural register-boundary repartition: there is no new
stage, execution stall, bypass source or retirement cycle.

All architectural WB consumers must use this same held result through
the existing wb_w_data connections: EX forwarding, same-cycle register
file bypass, register writes and RVFI rd_wdata. Keep raw dmem_rdata,
masks, address and store data separately for RVFI; never replace raw
rvfi_mem_rdata with an extended/selected result. Retain every instruction,
operand, PC and trap field and the existing MEM alignment checks.
A trapping load still suppresses its write exactly as before. Do not
gate result capture by valid, reg_write or rd!=0: preserve the original
WB mux's value even for bubbles and nonwriters, leaving eligibility to
existing control logic.

Reset clears result with the rest of MEM/WB. On hold_wb retain result,
rd and control while clearing valid only. This preserves forwarding
from an already-retired load while a later memory operation stalls:
MEM/WB.valid may be zero while its data remains an eligible source.
Preserve current registered forwarding matches, live qualification,
EX/MEM-over-WB priority and two-bit selector/data mux implementation.
Older instructions still drain during blocking multiply/divide and
saved RVFI operand semantics remain identical. Keep nret=1, all ports,
decoder legality, M-extension and ALTOPS schedules, predictor, fetch
FIFO, recovery latency and bus acceptance rules unchanged.

The intended gain is removal of the wide post-register WB mux and
roughly one 32-bit result register bank from the recurrent feedback
interface. The mux instead enters MEM's load-result input cone, where
memory extraction could become limiting. Gowin can also expose other
EX/divider paths, so the transformation does not guarantee acceptance.
Do not combine it with registered forwarding priority, one-hot operand
muxes, delayed branch recovery or validity-only payload changes.
Those were separate probes and did not outperform this focused design.

The exact selected-result-only prototype passed lint, both existing
real/ALTOPS pipeline builds, stalled reference/selftest cosimulation
and canonical stalled CoreMark validation. It measured Gowin placement
options 0/1/2 at 73.181/77.044/77.044 MHz, median 77.044 MHz, with
5,874 logic cells, 1,323 registers, 49 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs.

u_wb and still involve EX/recovery; option 1's leading arrival was

At unchanged 3,989,539 cycles this projects about 193.12 iterations/s,
approximately four percent above 185.62. This is BELOW the 4.6 percent
acceptance gate, not an accepted improvement. The strongest tested
structural angle therefore has an evidence-based expected gain of
four percent with low confidence, rather than an unsupported larger
claim. Full formal was stopped before completion for the proposal
time budget; no complete formal pass is claimed.

at 3,989,539 cycles. Reproduce actual bracketed CoreMark cycles and the
normal three-option median vendor timing after implementation. Run all
existing real/ALTOPS unit tests, unchanged single-channel formal with
liveness and strict order, stalled reference cosimulation, and canonical
CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks. Never weaken any assertion,
formal depth, decoder invariant or evaluation contract. Preserve this
single retiming focus; do not present a best placement or the subthreshold
prototype projection as an accepted fitness improvement.

title: Restrict predictor recovery to PC selection and narrow squash state
motivation:
The current champion reaches 185.62 iterations/s at 74.054 MHz and
3,989,539 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at
MEM/WB read_data and ends at the IF PC through WB and EX. After the
multiplier/divider improvements, predictor recovery is now a concrete
timing target. Prior predictor logs report roughly 52,000 conditional
misses and 13,735 JALRs, leaving limited accuracy-only headroom.

Carrying IF targets through the pipeline regressed in r7s2; moving all
branch verification to MEM failed liveness in r8s2; selective deferred
verification in r10s2 reduced cycles but lost frequency. Instead, keep
the existing prediction and EX verification schedule and remove the
serial full-width recovery-address selection before the IF PC register.
Local probes also expose the branch decision's fanout to fetch-queue
payload writes and ID/EX payload clearing as competing recovery paths.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Represent the fetch PC using one normal-prediction register, three
independent recovery-address registers, and a small registered source
selector. The three recovery candidates are the resolving instruction's
PC+4, its full PC+immediate direct target, and its full forwarded
(rs1+immediate)&~1 JALR target. EX exports these candidates independently
together with the existing accepted redirect pulse and a recovery kind.
A legal aligned actual transfer selects direct or indirect as appropriate;
a predicted-taken conditional branch that resolves not taken selects
fallthrough. Preserve all existing legality, target-alignment, acceptance,
training and architectural pc_next calculations.

In IF, select the current logical PC combinationally from these registered
banks, and use that same logical PC for imem_addr, fetch_packet.pc,
predictor indexing, direct-target arithmetic and PC+4. The selector has
NORMAL, FALLTHROUGH, DIRECT and INDIRECT states. Reset selects NORMAL
and resets its PC to RESET_PC. An accepted EX redirect captures the
appropriate recovery kind at the same edge that the independent banks
capture its candidate addresses. Redirect has priority over fetch_accept.
The corrected fetch address is visible immediately after this edge,
exactly as today: add no recovery bubble, pipeline stage or bus cycle.

Capture all three candidate banks UNCONDITIONALLY on every clock. This lets EX
compute each candidate into a register without selecting between full
addresses using the late forwarded branch result. In particular, the
JALR adder must terminate at its own candidate register, not a shared
redirect-target mux. The small selector alone encodes which registered
candidate is live. Do not put redirect, fetch acceptance or the current
selector on any candidate bank's clock enable or data mux. A conditional
capture would reconstruct the late branch-outcome-to-address-register
path that this hypothesis targets. Candidate payloads need
no reset because reset selects the initialized normal bank and every
later recovery selection has a simultaneous candidate capture.

On every non-reset edge write normal_pc_q <= fetch_accept ? next_pc : pc,
where pc is the currently selected logical PC. Independently write
pc_src_q <= redirect ? recovery_kind : NORMAL. Reset sets normal_pc_q
to RESET_PC and pc_src_q to NORMAL. Thus a recovery bank is selected for
one cycle, then its address transfers into the normal bank if fetch is
stalled; it need not remain selected for the duration of a stall. When
fetch is accepted, the normal bank instead receives that word's predicted
successor. A simultaneous new redirect overrides this normal-bank value
by selecting the freshly sampled recovery candidate. This also supports
consecutive redirects without relying on their reachability.

The resulting selected-PC transition is exactly reset ? RESET_PC :
redirect ? resolved_recovery_target : fetch_accept ? next_pc : old_pc.
Check this equality for every cycle, especially the cycle after recovery
when imem remains unready. Simply holding the normal register then would
restore a stale wrong-path PC. All externally
visible fetch addresses derive only from registered banks and selector;
never drive an address directly from live EX operands or imem_data.

Complete the same recovery isolation by separating squash state from
discarded payload data. In the four-entry queue, remove redirect from
the payload RAM write enable: allow !reset && enqueue to write even on
a recovery edge. Keep redirect's priority in count and pointer reset.
This speculative write is dead because the queue becomes empty; no
overwritten word becomes live before a subsequent enqueue initializes
its slot. Preserve the full-queue simultaneous pop/push behavior.

In ID, retain reset clearing and whole-packet hold under stall. Otherwise
capture the presented PC, operands, immediate, register addresses,
instruction and prediction regardless of flush or input validity. Set
ctrl to zero and valid to zero on flush or invalid input; capture decoded
controls and valid only for a live unflushed packet. Every control bit,
including memory enables and reg_write, must be zero in a bubble because
validity alone does not gate all consumers. Unused bubble payload may be
arbitrary, but must never launch arithmetic, redirect, train, write a
register, access memory or retire. This reduces late recovery fanout to
selection, occupancy, validity and control bits without changing latency.

Preserve the four-entry fall-through queue and its 66-bit packet format.
Redirect clears the entire queue and flushes ID/EX on the original edge,
regardless of bus readiness, while older instructions complete normally.
Leave queued predictions immutable. Keep the 64 persistent binary bimodal
counters, pre-edge lookup, delayed training event and saturation unchanged.
Do not move branch verification or training, change load-use interlocks,
add a target cache, or modify arithmetic execution. Preserve nret=1,
all top-level ports, full address width, decoder default-illegal behavior,
RVFI order/operands/PC/traps, memory handshakes and wrong-path suppression.

This is a predictor-recovery retiming hypothesis with an expected eight
percent fitness gain and low confidence, not a measured final result. It moves
address selection after independent registers without increasing branch
latency. Prediction decisions and bracketed cycles should remain exactly
unchanged. The extra address registers and post-register PC mux may shift
the critical path into IF prediction or add routing cost; synthesis may
also reconstruct shared muxes. Inspect the synthesized paths to establish
that the intended register boundary survives, rather than assuming RTL
structure guarantees a clock gain. Do not exploit wrapper-only behavior.

At unchanged 3,989,539 cycles, acceptance requires fitness above
194.15852 iterations/s, approximately 77.46 MHz median Gowin Fmax.

title: Balance the EX branch comparator into a LUT-sized reduction tree
motivation:
The champion scores 199.08 iterations/s at 79.422 MHz and 3,989,539
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs from
ID/EX.rs2_val[0] through EX to IF.pc[20], with 41 cells and 17.892 ns
arrival. A low operand bit reaching the redirect destination is
consistent with a full-width relational comparison on branch recovery.
Recent result-loop improvements have removed the former writeback mux
bottleneck. Prior forwarding-mux rewrites and recovery-address banking
failed to clear acceptance; neither directly shortened the branch
comparator itself. This proposal targets that local combinational cone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the EX conditional-branch comparison network with shared
equality and unsigned-less-than predicates built as a balanced tree.
Preserve the original forwarded rs1 and rs2, instruction schedule,
prediction, target calculation, recovery edge and training event.
This is a branch-comparator micro-optimization, not a prediction change.

Divide the 32-bit operands into sixteen two-bit slices. At each leaf
compute eq=(a_slice==b_slice) and lt=(a_slice<b_slice), both functions
of four input bits with bounded local comparison depth. Retain the
native two-bit relational expression rather than expanding it into
Boolean terms; that version gave the strongest measured mapping.
Combine adjacent
groups from most significant to least significant with
eq_parent=eq_hi && eq_lo and
lt_parent=lt_hi || (eq_hi && lt_lo).
Use four explicitly balanced reduction levels, never a linear priority
loop or a full-width subtraction. The root yields exact 32-bit equality
and unsigned less-than. For signed less-than use
(rs1[31]^rs2[31]) ? rs1[31] : unsigned_lt.
Decode the six existing BR_* cases from these shared predicates:
BEQ=eq, BNE=!eq, BLT=signed_lt, BGE=!signed_lt,
BLTU=unsigned_lt, BGEU=!unsigned_lt. Preserve the default-false case.
Do not alter the general ALU comparisons or introduce new pipeline state.

The intended gain comes from replacing a long operand-dependent
magnitude-comparison chain with shallow LUT logic before the existing
redirect controls. Keep every original branch_taken, actual_taken,
misalignment, redirect, redirect_target and train_valid equation and
every pipeline-register update intact. The direct and JALR address
adders, branch predictor, queue, forwarding selection, load-use stalls,
multiplier and divider remain unchanged. This gives a precise
cycle-for-cycle equivalence target, including arbitrary invalid bubbles.

Preserve nret=1 and all top-level ports, decoder default-illegal
discipline, misaligned-target traps, wrong-path suppression, bus holds,
RVFI source values, PC continuity and contiguous retirement order.
Check all six comparisons on equality, opposite signs, INT_MIN/MAX,
adjacent values and pairs whose highest differing bit is each position
from 0 through 31. Exhaustively check two-bit leaves and group-combine
truth tables, then random full-width operand pairs against the original
relational expressions. Exercise every forwarding-source combination,
youngest-writer priority, x0, both prediction-error directions and
prolonged independent imem/dmem stalls in pipeline verification.

A disposable prototype of precisely this two-bit-leaf tree and the
original six-case branch decode measured Gowin placement options
0/1/2 at 77.196/82.257/82.257 MHz, median 82.257 MHz. It used 5,856
logic cells, 1,323 FFs, 49 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs.
Canonical stalled CoreMark passed the unchanged CRC/UART/bounds,
completion and marker validator in exactly 3,989,539 bracketed cycles.
This projects 206.181717 iterations/s, a 3.567 percent improvement
over the champion's rounded 199.08. The integer impact estimate rounds
this to four percent; it is NOT evidence of tournament acceptance.
Acceptance requires more than 208.23768 iterations/s, approximately
83.07724 MHz at this cycle count. This prototype misses that threshold.

The prototype passed lint, all 36 existing pipeline tests in both the
ordinary and YOSYS-declaration builds, selftest reference cosimulation
with and without bus stalls, and the canonical CoreMark run. A Yosys
SAT miter proved the actual replacement branch_cond equal to the
original for every pair of 32-bit operands and every three-bit branch
operation, including both default-false encodings. This is exhaustive
combinational equivalence, not a claim of completing riscv-formal's
full sequential gate. The implementer must still pass every unchanged
formal and cosimulation gate and reproduce the scored vendor median.

Competing EX result and recovery-control paths limit the measured gain.
Larger comparison slices, altered signed/polarity factoring, explicit
Boolean leaves and moving selection after speculative comparisons did
not improve on this tree. Registering complete forwarding selectors
also failed to improve it. Do not bundle those alternatives into this
proposal. Keep this single branch-comparator change and report its
actual acceptance outcome honestly; no above-threshold gain is claimed.
All temporary working RTL edits were restored after measurement.

title: Fuse load-to-branch execution through a registered comparison stage
motivation:
The champion achieves 199.08 iterations/s at 79.422 MHz and 3,989,539
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst path now runs from an ID/EX operand
through EX branch resolution to the fetch PC. A local run of the
unchanged champion with the standard instruction/data stalls reproduced
exactly 3,989,539 bracketed cycles. Streaming its retirement trace found
135,320 adjacent true load-to-branch dependencies, versus only 8,949
load-to-simple-ALU dependencies. Load-to-branch execution is therefore a
materially larger throughput opportunity than general late ALU execution.

Structural r11s1's isolated writeback retiming gained only 4.04 percent;
r11s0 removed its companion EX result mux and exposed recovery timing.
Earlier branch-only direct MEM-to-EX forwarding saved cycles but lost
frequency in r7s0. Selective MEM verification in r10s2 avoided the raw
memory feedback path but placed operand repair and comparison on the
recovery cycle and lost frequency. Moving every branch to MEM in r8s2
failed bounded liveness. The proposed load/branch pair instead performs
comparison early and registers its decision before frontend recovery,
while independent branches retain their original schedule.
