hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a dedicated load-to-branch comparison lane spanning the existing
EX/MEM boundary. Admit a legal conditional branch immediately behind a
load it consumes, without the current load-use bubble. While that load
is in MEM and the branch is in EX, compare the accepted, correctly
extended load response against the branch's other forwarded operand.
Capture the outcome and original prediction with the branch in EX/MEM.
In the following cycle recover and train from those registered bits.
This is one structural change to execution placement: form a load/branch
pair with a register between comparison and recovery. Prediction policy,
independent-branch resolution and all other instruction latencies stay
unchanged. Do not defer the comparison itself to MEM/WB forwarding.

Restrict admission to positively decoded legal BRANCH encodings whose
source matches the preceding valid load's nonzero destination. Exempt
these branches from the one-cycle load-use interlock; retain all other
interlocks. In EX identify the pair against the actual older EX/MEM load
and latch a paired-branch bit only when the branch advances. Backpressure
from that load still holds both stages until io_dmemReady is asserted.
An instruction-bus stall or empty fetch queue cannot invent a pair.
Independent conditional branches, JAL and JALR still resolve in EX.

Export MEM's existing byte/halfword/word extraction and sign extension
as a combinational internal load value, together with actual load-write
qualification after alignment/trap checking. Supply that value only to
the dedicated pair comparator and its captured RVFI source values. For
each matching branch source use the load value if the load really writes
that nonzero register. For a trapping misaligned load, use the youngest
older architectural value: a matching retained MEM/WB writer, otherwise
the ID/EX operand. Exclude the pending load's EX/MEM alu_result, which is
an address, from this fallback. Handle either or both branch operands
matching the load. Unmatched operands retain ordinary forwarding.
MEM/WB forwarding qualification must retain today's behavior when valid
clears but its data/control remain available during a data stall.

Implement a separate six-condition comparator for the paired lane so
raw load data never enters the normal EX branch-to-IF path. Compute its
EQ, signed ordering and unsigned ordering from the repaired operands.
Its decision terminates at EX/MEM outcome/fault/prediction metadata,
not at IF PC selection, queue reset, ID squash or predictor RAM writes.
Register the full direct target and branch PC independently of that
decision, reusing existing EX/MEM fields. MEM recovery chooses the
registered target or registered PC plus four from registered outcome
bits. Avoid using an outcome-selected wide PC register as the timed
destination of the raw-load comparator. RVFI-only resolved pc_next may
be captured conventionally; derive timed recovery from the separate
registered candidates and decision. Keep full 32-bit address arithmetic.

Check target alignment exactly as today: a taken misaligned target traps,
suppresses the architectural transfer and continues at PC+4; a not-taken
branch with an unaligned encoded target remains legal. Carry corrected
original source values, resolved next PC, trap controls and instruction
identity through normal retirement. Suppress EX redirect and training
for paired branches. In MEM an accepted paired branch compares its saved
prediction with its saved legal aligned actual-taken bit, then emits
recovery and eligible conditional training once. Unrelated dmem-not-ready
cannot hold this branch because its MEM packet has no memory request.
Normal ALU, multiply, divide, memory-address and store-data paths do not
consume the new raw-load forwarding signal.

An older paired-branch MEM correction wins over all younger EX activity.
It advances the branch to WB, discards the fetch queue, flushes ID/EX and
installs an inert EX/MEM bubble instead of the younger EX instruction.
Gate younger multiply/divide launch, redirect, training and acceptance
with this older kill. Kill must win over a wrong-path execute_wait;
clearing valid alone is insufficient because controls also drive memory
enables and forwarding. Older work still retires once, and no wrong-path
memory operation reaches EX/MEM. Preserve ordinary dmem hold priorities
when no older correction exists. Correctly predicted paired branches
allow younger execution to continue normally.

Feed the existing single registered predictor-training interface with
accepted MEM-pair learning ahead of accepted EX-branch learning. If both
eligible events coincide on a correct path, deliberately discard only
the younger advisory EX learning event, as in the earlier selective
verification design; do not stall execution or add a second table port.
Never train a squashed instruction. Preserve the current counter table,
indexing, reset retention, saturation and pre-edge prediction semantics.
Account for this explicit collision policy when comparing cycle counts.

The schedule is essential: with zero wait states, the old load-use bubble
places the dependent branch in EX on the same cycle that the new paired
branch reaches MEM. Thus its registered recovery is available on the
original recovery cycle. A correct prediction saves a bubble; a miss
does not acquire the additional recovery cycle of the failed all-MEM
design. On a stalled load, sample the comparison only at its accepted
response edge. This timing argument does not replace the unchanged
liveness proof; keep every formal bound and assumption intact.

Estimate a seven percent fitness improvement with low confidence. The
measured 135,320 adjacent dependencies represent at most 3.39 percent
of current cycles, not a guaranteed saving: bus stalls and predictions
change the realized schedule. At three percent fewer cycles, acceptance
above 208.23768 iterations/s requires about 80.585 MHz median Fmax, only
1.46 percent above the champion. Registering the early comparison is
intended to avoid the frequency losses of both earlier unregistered
memory forwarding and late WB-repair/comparison. Added comparator area,
load-data fanout, recovery arbitration, and the unchanged ordinary EX
branch path may still prevent acceptance. No implementation, timing or
correctness result is claimed for this final paired design.

Preliminary alternatives were rejected rather than included: a parallel
forwarding-source comparator bank passed all 36 pipeline tests and a
combinational equivalence proof but measured only 72.148 MHz in Gowin
placement option 1. Registered queue-recovery bookkeeping also failed
to establish a gain. The final hypothesis is the load/branch execution
pairing above, not either measured below-threshold alternative.

Preserve nret=1, every top-level IO, decoder default-illegal behavior,
RV32M/ALTOPS behavior, memory handshakes and all RVFI invariants. Validate
the pair's temporal behavior and exact architectural traces with unit
tests, unchanged formal including liveness, and stalled cosimulation.
Run canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks and every scored
Gowin placement option. Inspect both raw-load-to-decision-register and
ordinary/deferred recovery paths; evaluate the product of measured
iterations/cycle and median Fmax, not isolated clock or bubble savings.

title: Isolate predictor verification from arithmetic readiness and late polarity selection
motivation:
The champion scores 199.08 iterations/s at 79.422 MHz and 3,989,539 measured CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path starts at an ID/EX branch operand and reaches the IF PC. The present verification path selects among six branch predicates, applies taken-target fault qualification, compares against the prediction and selects a correction address using the resolved outcome. Much of that work depends only on instruction metadata and the captured prediction, so it can be prepared independently of the late operands.

Prior target-carrying, deferred verification and recovery-bank designs failed to clear acceptance or failed liveness. Local probes confirmed that simply segmenting the comparator or moving a correction address into ID does not suffice, and registering the recovery event fails the unchanged liveness check. Keep the existing recovery edge and instead specialize its predicate around the original prediction.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predecode one bit of prediction-verification metadata in ID: branch_recover_invert = original predicted_taken XOR decoded branch_op[0]. Add this bit to ID/EX only, before the trailing instruction/prediction/valid fields so the existing low-bit packet conventions remain intact. Capture it atomically with the instruction, hold it on all existing stalls and clear it with the existing complete bubble/reset. Do not alter the 66-bit IF packet or four-entry fetch FIFO. This prepares BEQ/BNE and LT/GE inversion plus prediction polarity before forwarded operand comparison.

In EX replace the separate signed/unsigned branch relational expressions with one shared unsigned comparison. Transform each forwarded operand's most-significant bit by XOR with !branch_op[1], leaving bits 30:0 unchanged; compare the resulting 32-bit unsigned words. For BLT/BGE this flips the sign bit in both operands and exactly implements signed ordering, while BLTU/BGEU leave both words unchanged. Independently compute equality of the original operands. Set base_predicate = branch_op[2] ? shared_less : equal. For each of the six legal branch funct3 values, architectural branch_cond = base_predicate XOR branch_op[0]; preserve default false for reserved values. Do not change the ALU's SLT/SLTU operations or any forwarding mux.

Compute conditional prediction mismatch directly as base_predicate XOR the saved branch_recover_invert. Qualify this with branch eligibility prepared independently of the condition: !is_illegal && direct_target[1:0]==0. The conditional recovery term is is_branch && ((eligible && mismatch) || (!eligible && predicted_taken)). The second term keeps recovery to fallthrough explicit even for a captured taken prediction whose transfer is ineligible. A not-taken branch with an unaligned encoded target remains legal, trains not taken and does not redirect when predicted not taken. Keep architectural misalign_branch, misalign_jump, ctrl_with_trap and branch_taken calculations unchanged.

Keep jump recovery separate from conditional comparison. Define jump_eligible = !is_illegal && !misalign_jump. The direct-JAL term is is_jump && !is_jalr && (predicted_taken != jump_eligible). The JALR term is is_jump && is_jalr && jump_eligible. OR these with the conditional term and apply a predictor-specific control_accept = !reset && in.valid && !stall. Remove execute_wait only from the acceptance used by recovery and predictor training: a positively decoded BRANCH, JAL or JALR always has base ALU_ADD and can never be a blocking MUL/DIV operation. Conversely, every blocking M instruction has is_branch=is_jump=is_jalr=0, so it cannot redirect or train even though control_accept ignores its wait. Do not remove execute_wait from real execution, pipeline holds or any arithmetic handshake. This static instruction-class exclusion cuts the ALU/divider readiness-to-predictor path without changing the event sequence. Preserve !stall so an older unready data-memory operation still defers control-flow acceptance. Use only jump-specific alignment to qualify jumps; do not route a conditional branch predicate through a shared actual_taken/misalign_fault expression into the jump terms. Decoded branch and jump classes are mutually exclusive. Use control_accept also for train_valid, retaining the original is_branch, actual condition, illegal and target-fault qualifications. Thus accepted training remains exactly once and on the original cycle for every reachable decoded instruction.

Select the correction address independently of the resolved condition: for JALR use the existing full forwarded (rs1+immediate)&~1 sum; otherwise use predicted_taken ? PC+4 : PC+immediate. On an accepted direct-control mismatch this is exactly the alternative to the captured prediction, including fallthrough recovery for an ineligible taken prediction. The target is irrelevant when redirect is false. Keep architectural EX/MEM.pc_next, link values and trap write suppression resolved exactly as before; never substitute a speculative or alternative address into RVFI pc_wdata. No additional target register or post-register PC mux is required.

Add no recovery cycle, pipeline stage, annul protocol, load-use optimization or arithmetic change. title: Predecode branch predicates and multiplier sign bits at operand capture
motivation:
The champion scores 199.08 iterations/s at 79.422 MHz and 3,989,539
bracketed CoreMark cycles. The r12s0 balanced branch comparator gained
3.57 percent but missed acceptance because competing EX paths remained.
Local timing also exposes multiplier operation decoding before its
DSP inputs. Precomputing execution-mode decisions at the existing
operand-capture boundaries can shorten both paths without extra cycles.
Branch predecode alone measured 81.217 MHz in placement option 1;
multiplier sign capture alone measured 79.427 MHz. The combination
measured a scored median of 84.388 MHz across all three placement options.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Apply one EX control-predecode micro-optimization at the existing
branch and multiply operand-capture boundaries. Preserve every stage,
instruction latency, forwarding rule and recovery event. Use a balanced
branch comparison with the predecoded controls; retain native base ALU
arithmetic and every original target/address adder.

Add four bits to id_ex_t immediately before instr: branch_eq,
branch_signed, branch_unsigned and branch_invert. In ID capture them
from dec_branch_op by testing membership in {BEQ,BNE}, {BLT,BGE},
{BLTU,BGEU}, and {BNE,BGE,BGEU}, respectively. Capture atomically with
the operands, hold on every existing stall and clear on reset, flush
or invalid-input bubbles. Keep ctrl_t, the IF packet and trailing
instr/predicted_taken/valid ordering unchanged. Decoder default-illegal
behavior and positively validated opcode/funct matches remain intact.

In EX compare the original forwarded rs1 and rs2 using sixteen native
two-bit equality and unsigned-less-than leaves. Combine adjacent
groups in an explicitly balanced four-level tree. A higher-significance
group H and lower group L produce eq=eq_H&&eq_L and
lt=lt_H||(eq_H&&lt_L). Keep native two-bit relational leaves; the prior
comparator experiment found them better than Boolean expansion.
Derive signed_less=(rs1[31]^rs2[31]) ? rs1[31] : unsigned_less.
Replace the late six-case predicate selection with
  branch_cond = ((in.branch_eq && equal) ||
                 (in.branch_signed && signed_less) ||
                 (in.branch_unsigned && unsigned_less))
                ^ in.branch_invert;
Reserved branch-op values predecode to four zero bits, preserving
default false. Cleared bubble flags remain inert. Preserve the original
six predicates for every positively decoded branch instruction.

At the multiplier's existing request-capture edge, capture alongside
mul_a_q and mul_b_q:
  mul_sign_a_q = (op==ALU_MULH || op==ALU_MULHSU) && a[31];
  mul_sign_b_q = (op==ALU_MULH) && b[31];
  mul_low_q = (op==ALU_MUL);
Reset these bits with multiply state. Update them only on the original
accepted request and hold throughout pending completion/backpressure.
Form the real signed 33-bit DSP operands directly from
{mul_sign_a_q,mul_a_q} and {mul_sign_b_q,mul_b_q}. Select product[31:0]
versus product[63:32] with mul_low_q. Preserve the single signed 66-bit
product and exact RV32M results. Remove operation decode and live sign
gating between the operand registers and DSP; do not change the
multiplier algorithm or introduce another arithmetic register stage.

Keep mul_op_q and the existing captured-operand formulas under
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS. Real-only metadata may be compiled out in ALTOPS.
Preserve capture at edge one, earliest transfer at edge two, every
ready/valid signal, reset cancellation and held-result stability.

Keep all forwarding muxes/selectors, base ALU operations, address and
target adders, divider arithmetic/schedule, queues and predictor state
unchanged. In particular retain ex_accept INCLUDING !execute_wait,
branch_taken, actual_taken, alignment checks, misalign_fault, redirect,
redirect_target, training and architectural pc_next equations. Do not
alter prediction polarity, move branch resolution or narrow pipeline
bubble clears. Preserve retained WB forwarding, youngest-writer priority,
x0, nret=1, all top-level/RVFI ports, precise operands/PCs/traps and
contiguous retirement order. No evaluation or contract files change.

A disposable combined prototype measured Gowin placement options 0/1/2
at 78.972/84.388/84.388 MHz, median 84.388 MHz. Option 0 used 5,850
logic cells, 1,256 registers, 49 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs.
Canonical stalled CoreMark passed the unchanged CRC/UART/bounds,
completion and marker validator in exactly 3,989,539 bracketed cycles.
These measurements yield 211.523186 iterations/s, 6.2503 percent above
the rounded champion score of 199.08. They exceed the 208.23768
acceptance threshold. This is prototype evidence, not orchestrator
acceptance; the implementation must reproduce the median and pass
every unchanged correctness gate. Neither isolated control change met
this margin. Routing and competing EX/divider paths remain risks.

An exhaustive Yosys SAT miter proved the balanced branch tree and
predecoded selection equivalent to the original predicates for every
operand pair and all eight branch-op encodings. The combined prototype
passed both existing pipeline-test variants and stalled selftest
reference cosimulation (115 retirements). Its byte-identical modified
ALU passed the existing real and ALTOPS test suites, including exact
multiply arithmetic, capture/hold/transfer timing and live input changes
after capture. Full sequential riscv-formal was not run during this
proposal; no full formal pass is claimed. Add directed checks for the
new metadata capture/hold/clear and run unchanged full formal,
especially liveness, reg, pc_fwd and unique, stalled reference cosimulation
and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks. Confirm identical
bracketed cycles and use every scored Gowin placement option. Never
weaken assertions, formal depths or verification contracts.

title: Partition EX into operand-candidate arithmetic slices
motivation: The champion scores 199.08 iterations/s at 79.422 MHz and 3,989,539 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior r8s1 registered address matches but retained live qualification and priority before arithmetic. The r12 balanced comparator gained only 3.57 percent because arithmetic and recovery paths competed. Local probes confirm that retiming routing alone leaves these paths dominant, while replicating whole ALUs creates excessive area and routing. A structural execution fabric that selects narrow arithmetic summaries before one shared carry tree targets both limitations without extra instruction latency.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion scores 199.08 iterations/s at 79.422 MHz and 3,989,539 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior r8s1 registered address matches but retained live qualification and priority before arithmetic. The r12 balanced comparator gained only 3.57 percent because arithmetic and recovery paths competed. Local probes confirm that retiming routing alone leaves these paths dominant, while replicating whole ALUs creates excessive area and routing. A structural execution fabric that selects narrow arithmetic summaries before one shared carry tree targets both limitations without extra instruction latency.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the shared mux-then-wide-arithmetic EX topology with a bank of narrow operand-candidate arithmetic slices and one shared carry-prefix network. Register complete operand routes before EX so their matching and priority work is not chained through arithmetic. This is one structural redesign of operand delivery and base execution; preserve the five-stage schedule, one-retire interface, predictor, fetch queue, load-use bubble, memory protocol and blocking M-extension schedules.

First compute exact next-cycle producer identities and write eligibility at the current ID/EX boundary. Retain the existing next_rs1/next_rs2, next_ex_rd and next_wb_rd rules. Next EX/MEM reg_write is its held value on dmem stall, zero on an EX bubble or execute_wait, otherwise the actual post-trap control that EX will capture. Next MEM/WB reg_write is its held value on hold_mem_wb, otherwise MEM's post-alignment/trap control. Do not gate retained WB eligibility with retirement valid. Expose these controls internally, without guessing from opcodes or ignoring faults.

Resolve nonzero-source matches, actual write eligibility and youngest EX/MEM priority over MEM/WB before the edge. Register one-hot raw routes: saved ID/EX operand, EX/MEM result, or MEM/WB result. Refresh them every edge, including consumer holds, because producers can drain. Also register four-way ALU routes, incorporating PC for AUIPC and immediate for alu_src before the edge. Use actual incoming decoded controls, or retained ID/EX controls during a hold. Reset routes to saved operand. Flushed/invalid consumers retain inert pipeline controls; unused route metadata may reflect the presented head, like existing match flags, and is refreshed before another valid consumer executes. Do not add recovery fanout merely to sanitize unused route bits. Remove obsolete match registers and post-edge priority/qualification logic.

In the new combinational execution fabric, ALU A has four candidate words: saved rs1, EX/MEM result, MEM/WB result and PC. ALU B has saved rs2, EX/MEM result, MEM/WB result and immediate. Partition every candidate into eight four-bit slices. For ADD use B unchanged and initial carry zero; for SUB, SLT, SLTU and conditional-branch comparison use complemented B and initial carry one. The conditional-branch flag selects subtraction for the comparison fabric even though the existing decoder's branch alu_op is ADD. Branch instructions never write the ALU result, so their arithmetic value is unused; preserve raw operands and all architectural branch/link/trap calculations.

For each slice and each candidate pair compute only local five-bit sums for carry-in zero and one, plus carry-generate and carry-propagate: t0={0,a4}+{0,b4_effective}, s0=t0[3:0], s1=(t0+1)[3:0], g=t0[4], p=AND(a4 XOR b4_effective). All widths must be explicit, and s1 is a local four-bit increment, not a serial inter-slice carry. Compute equality of the original uncomplemented candidate nibbles alongside these summaries. Select s0/s1/g/p/equality with the registered one-hot A/B routes, using balanced masked reductions or a factored two-dimensional selection. Constant-identical candidates may share logic. Do not build sixteen full-width ALUs, multipliers or shifters, and do not reintroduce a wide operand mux ahead of the local arithmetic.

Combine the eight selected (g,p) summaries with a balanced three-level parallel-prefix network. For adjacent high and low groups use G=G_high OR (P_high AND G_low), P=P_high AND P_low. Compute each nibble boundary carry from its prefix and initial carry, then select that nibble's already-computed s0 or s1. Never ripple eight nibble carries or use a 32-bit final correction adder. This shares wide carry propagation AFTER candidate selection instead of repeating it for every operand pair. Keep full modulo-2^32 arithmetic and expose the final subtraction carry for comparisons.

Use the same subtraction summaries for unsigned less-than, equal and signed less-than: unsigned_less is the inverse of final carry, equality is the balanced AND of selected original-nibble equalities, and signed_less selects A's sign when original operand signs differ, otherwise unsigned_less. For the six legal branch conditions choose equal/not-equal, signed_less/not-signed_less, or unsigned_less/not-unsigned_less. Preserve default-false handling of reserved branch selectors. ADD/SUB results and SLT/SLTU bits feed the ordinary base result. LUI, Boolean operations and shifts remain single shared operations on shallow one-hot-selected ALU operands; replicate none of those wide functions.

Keep raw rs1/rs2 selectors separate from PC/immediate overrides for RVFI, stores, M-extension capture and the dedicated full rs1-plus-immediate address path. Do not alter the divider, multiplier or their real/ALTOPS arithmetic and latency. Integrate the new base result without leaving a second live conventional wide ADD/SUB/comparison path selected in parallel. One option is a default-disabled external-base-result mode on alu.sv: standalone ALU tests keep its original interface behavior, while EX enables the new execution fabric and the ALU still owns the unchanged M-extension handshakes. Add internal ports or a new RTL module as needed; external core ports remain unchanged.

The structural benefit is that register routing resolves before EX, candidate arithmetic is only four bits wide, and a single balanced prefix handles carry and branch ordering. The same mechanism shortens the competing arithmetic and recovery operand paths. Estimated fitness gain is eight percent, low confidence. Acceptance requires more than 208.23768 iterations/s, approximately 83.08 MHz at unchanged 3,989,539 cycles. Candidate-summary selection fanout, added LUTs, synthesis refactoring and untouched M-extension paths may defeat the gain. Target comfortably below 10,000 logic cells; inspect inferred structure and all scored Gowin placement options.

Preliminary probes are negative evidence, not measurements of this final fabric. Moving older forwarding into ID operands reached 76.220 MHz median. Replicating complete arithmetic and branch functions reached 67.618 MHz and 11,456 logic cells. Registering complete one-hot raw/ALU routes alone reached 76.496 MHz, with arithmetic/recovery paths still critical; its adapted pipeline tests, all 53 unchanged formal checks, and stalled reference/CoreMark cosimulation passed. None clears acceptance. The final narrow-slice/shared-prefix execution fabric has not been implemented or timed. Its prediction must be verified rather than inferred from those probes.

Validate all route transitions and candidate pairs, carry/borrow crossing every nibble boundary, all-zero/all-one operands, signed extrema, opposite signs, equality and differing low nibbles. Compare randomized ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU results and every branch predicate to independent 32-bit reference arithmetic, including PC/immediate routes. Preserve existing assertions while adapting internal selector encodings with exact one-hot/value checks. Test competing writers, x0, trapped JAL/JALR and loads, retained WB data, load-use bubbles, all holds/flush/reset transitions and M waits with draining producers. Run unchanged formal including liveness/reg/unique/pc_fwd, real and ALTOPS unit tests, stalled reference cosim and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks. Require unchanged bracketed cycles and median vendor timing for final evaluation.

title: Parallel balanced branch-verification lanes with predecoded recovery polarity
motivation:
The champion scores 199.08 iterations/s at 79.422 MHz and 3,989,539 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at an ID/EX branch operand and ends at the IF PC. The current verifier first selects two 32-bit forwarded operands, then compares them and qualifies recovery. Branch comparison also loads the same forwarded operand nets used by the general ALU.

Prior r12s0 comparator balancing reached only 82.257 MHz, while r12s2 early prediction polarity and recovery qualification reached only 79.243 MHz. Neither cleared acceptance. Replace that shared data-mux-then-compare topology with parallel balanced comparisons of forwarding candidates, selecting only one-bit predicates; predecode recovery polarity so the saved selection feeds a short mismatch path. This is one integrated predictor-verification topology, retaining the current prediction policy and recovery edge.

An advisory retirement-order CoreMark model found 51,419 direction misses for the current 64-entry bimodal organization versus 39,844 for a folded 256-entry table among 529,588 timed conditional branches. The architectural trace contains only 13,735 JALRs. These are trace-model counts, not cycle-accurate prediction results, and suggest limited cycle-saving headroom from a larger direction table or return stack. The proposed gain instead targets the observed verification timing bottleneck.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the existing predictor-verification cone with parallel, balanced comparison lanes over the possible forwarding sources, followed by one-bit source selection and predecoded prediction mismatch. Keep the 64 persistent bimodal counters, registered training event, direct JAL prediction, four-entry fall-through fetch queue, instruction schedule and EX recovery edge. This is one predictor-resolution redesign; leave arithmetic execution and architectural operand forwarding unchanged.

Add branch_recover_invert to id_ex_t immediately before its trailing instr, predicted_taken and valid fields. Preserve the current low-bit packet conventions and the unchanged 66-bit if_id_t/FIFO. ID captures original predicted_taken XOR decoded branch_op[0]. Hold and clear this bit atomically with the existing ID/EX packet. This folds the BEQ/BNE and LT/GE polarity together with the original prediction before operand comparison.

Retain the original EX rs1/rs2 forwarding muxes for the ALU, effective address, JALR, stores and RVFI operands. Build separate branch candidate arrays: A0=in.rs1_val, A1=fwd_ex_mem, A2=fwd_mem_wb; B0=in.rs2_val, B1=fwd_ex_mem, B2=fwd_mem_wb. For comparison only, XOR every candidate's bit 31 with !branch_op[1], leaving its low 31 bits intact. B1 and B2 share A1 and A2 after this transform. Signed BLT/BGE thereby become unsigned ordering on sign-flipped words; BLTU/BGEU remain unchanged. Equality is invariant. Perform this sign transform before the comparison trees, not as a signed-result mux after their roots.

Use seven real source-pair comparison lanes: 00, 01, 02, 10, 12, 20 and 21. For each pair, divide the transformed words into sixteen two-bit slices ordered most significant first. Use native two-bit equality and unsigned less-than at each leaf. Combine high/low groups through four explicitly balanced levels: eq_parent=eq_high AND eq_low; lt_parent=lt_high OR (eq_high AND lt_low). A convenient exact layout uses tree[16+k] for bits [31-2*k -: 2], k=0..15, and parent k combines 2*k and 2*k+1 for k=1..15. Do not substitute full-width comparisons, subtraction, or a serial priority chain. Each lane's base result is branch_op[2] ? root_lt : root_eq. Pairs 11 and 22 compare the same physical producer against itself; set their base result directly to !branch_op[2] (equality true, less-than false), with no comparator.

Decode each existing fwd_rs*_sel into three mutually exclusive enables: selector 1 chooses source 1, selector 2 source 2, and both 0 and 3 choose original source 0, matching the original forwarding case default. For pair ai,bi, enable=select_a[ai] AND select_b[bi]. Number lanes 3*ai+bi. Select only the one-bit base results: mask lanes 0..7 with their enables and OR them through a balanced eight-leaf reduction, then OR the enabled lane-8 result. This yields base_predicate without putting either 32-bit forwarding mux ahead of the branch comparator. Keep the original EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority supplied by forward_unit. Do not add valid gating to retained MEM/WB forwarding; its held data remains a legitimate source during a data stall.

For the six legal branch_op values, architectural branch_cond=base_predicate XOR branch_op[0]; default false for reserved branch_op values. Feed branch_cond into the original architectural branch_taken, target-fault, training outcome and resolved pc_next calculations. Compute conditional prediction mismatch directly as base_predicate XOR branch_recover_invert. Independently prepare direct_eligible=!is_illegal AND direct_target[1:0]==0. Conditional recovery is is_branch AND ((direct_eligible AND mismatch) OR (!direct_eligible AND predicted_taken)). This includes fallthrough correction for an ineligible taken prediction. A not-taken branch whose encoded target is misaligned remains legal and trains not taken; taken target faults retain their existing trap and linear architectural PC behavior.

Separate jump recovery from conditional comparison. Let jump_eligible=!is_illegal AND !misalign_jump. Direct-JAL recovery is is_jump AND !is_jalr AND (predicted_taken != jump_eligible); indirect recovery is is_jump AND is_jalr AND jump_eligible. OR these with conditional recovery and qualify by control_accept=!reset AND in.valid AND !stall. Omit execute_wait only from this predictor-specific acceptance: every positively decoded branch/JAL/JALR uses base ALU_ADD and is mutually exclusive with blocking MUL/DIV. Keep execute_wait in all real pipeline holds and arithmetic handshakes. A held M operation has no branch/jump classification and cannot redirect or learn. Retain !stall so older data-memory backpressure defers control-flow acceptance. Use control_accept for the original conditional-branch training enable, retaining legality and target-fault qualifications. Training still occurs exactly once at the original edge and carries the real branch condition.

Select the correction address independently of the late predicate. JALR retains the full forwarded (rs1+immediate)&~1 target; direct control uses predicted_taken ? PC+4 : PC+immediate. This selects the alternative to the original direct prediction whenever recovery is asserted; it is irrelevant otherwise. Keep architectural EX/MEM.pc_next, misalignment traps, link values and RVFI source values resolved exactly as before. Never use speculative correction metadata as the retiring architectural PC.

Keep the original IF PC register, recovery priority, complete younger-queue squash and ID/EX bubble on the current EX edge. Preserve load-use interlocks, independent bus backpressure, complete bubble controls, retained WB forwarding, decoder default-illegal behavior, nret=1 and all IO/RVFI ports. Add no recovery or verification cycle and do not change liveness bounds. Prediction decisions, accepted recoveries, learning and retirements must retain exactly the champion's cycle sequence.

A disposable implementation of this final topology measured Gowin placement options 0/1/2 at 79.416/83.648/83.648 MHz, median 83.648 MHz. It used 6,211 logic cells, 1,324 FFs, 49 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. This projects 209.668335 iterations/s, 5.319 percent above the rounded 199.08 champion, exceeding the 208.23768 acceptance threshold. The integer impact estimate rounds to five percent. This is a measured temporary-prototype result, not a completed orchestrator acceptance; the implementer must reproduce it and pass every unchanged gate.

The final prototype passed both existing test_pipeline.py pytest invocations (ordinary and YOSYS declarations), all selftest/random-program reference cosimulations with and without imem/dmem stalls, and canonical stalled CoreMark. Comparator replication increases area and routing, and the general ALU remains a competing critical path. Local ablations explain why the complete topology matters: parallel full-width comparison lanes with original recovery control reached only 75.917 MHz; a single balanced tree with predecoded recovery but after the shared operand muxes reached 80.046 MHz. Do not simplify the final seven balanced lanes back into either measured subthreshold topology. These ablations are evidence for this single integrated verifier, not additional proposed categories or variants.

title: Seed branch comparison with its predicate before balanced reduction
motivation:
The champion scores 211.52 iterations/s at 84.388 MHz with 3,989,539 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path carries forwarded WB data through EX branch recovery into IF. The accepted r13s0 comparator already has native two-bit leaves and balanced reduction, but still selects signed versus unsigned ordering, selects equality versus ordering, and applies polarity after wide comparison. Move those predicate choices to the leaves of the existing comparator, without replicating the comparator or changing prediction.

Prior larger comparison slices, registered forwarding routes and replicated arithmetic have not consistently improved vendor timing. Local probes against this champion also failed to improve it: removing queue recovery gating reached 82.310 MHz in placement option 1, narrowing ID squash reached 81.242 MHz, and predecoded ALU result selection reached 84.008 MHz. These are rejected probes and are not proposed changes.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the conditional-branch comparator in ex_stage.sv with a predicate-seeded balanced reduction. Preserve the existing four captured branch flags, all forwarding, original branch/redirect/training equations and every pipeline edge. This is a local Boolean topology optimization, with no prediction-policy or instruction-schedule change.

Use the original forwarded rs1 and rs2. Form cmp_a={rs1[31] XOR in.branch_signed,rs1[30:0]} and cmp_b analogously. Flipping both sign bits converts signed ordering to unsigned ordering; equality is unchanged. Let ordered=in.branch_signed OR in.branch_unsigned. Keep sixteen native two-bit comparisons and the same four balanced high/low reduction levels.

For each leaf k covering bits [2*k +: 2], compute p[k]=(cmp_a_slice==cmp_b_slice). For k>0 compute g[k]=ordered AND (cmp_a_slice<cmp_b_slice). For the least-significant leaf k=0, compute g[0]=(ordered AND (cmp_a_slice<cmp_b_slice)) OR (in.branch_eq AND p[0]). Thus an equality branch seeds the tree with equality at its low end while suppressing every ordering term. An ordering branch seeds it with ordinary unsigned less-than on sign-conditioned words. Combine a more-significant group H with a less-significant group L using P=P_H AND P_L and G=G_H OR (P_H AND G_L). Use an explicit balanced tree, e.g. leaves 16+k and parents 1..15 with child 2*k+1 more significant than child 2*k.

The root G is already the selected positive predicate: equality for BEQ/BNE, signed less-than for BLT/BGE, and unsigned less-than for BLTU/BGEU. Set branch_cond=root_G XOR in.branch_invert. All-zero predicate flags yield zero, preserving reserved/default behavior; the six legal modes retain their exact comparisons. Remove the old root signed-result mux and three-way predicate selection. Do not change branch predecode, target/address adders, misalignment handling, actual_taken, ex_accept (including !execute_wait), redirect, redirect_target, training, link values or architectural pc_next. All unused bubble controls and all register-update priorities remain unchanged.

This moves instruction-mode logic ahead of the reduction instead of behind its latest operand-dependent result. Only the top two-bit leaf needs sign conditioning, while equality needs no separate wide late selection. Native two-bit relational expressions should remain native; do not expand them into long bitwise priority chains or replace the tree with subtraction. Keep the original ALU, multiplier, divider, predictor counters and fetch queue. No new pipeline registers or execution/recovery cycles are required.

A disposable prototype of precisely this comparator measured placement options 0/1/2 at 83.122/84.473/84.473 MHz, median 84.473 MHz, versus the champion's 84.388 MHz. It uses 5,781 logic cells, 1,256 registers, 49 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Canonical stalled CoreMark passes the unchanged CRC/UART/bounds/completion/marker validator in exactly 3,989,539 bracketed cycles. This projects 211.736243 iterations/s, about 0.102 percent above the rounded 211.52 champion. The required integer impact estimate rounds to zero. It does NOT meet the 4.6 percent acceptance margin: that requires more than 221.24992 iterations/s, or approximately 88.26852 MHz. This is the strongest measured local micro-optimization in this proposal session, not an above-threshold candidate. Competing forwarding, ALU and divider paths limit the gain.

Both existing pipeline-test variants passed all 37 cocotb tests each without assertion changes. Stalled selftest reference cosimulation passed. An exhaustive Yosys SAT miter using the actual replacement expressions proved equality with the original six branch predicates for every operand pair and all eight branch-op encodings. These results establish local correctness and observed performance, not completed orchestrator acceptance. The implementation must still reproduce the result and pass every unchanged gate. A probe that additionally changed recovery qualification and saved prediction polarity reached only 81.220 MHz in options 1/2 and is explicitly excluded.

Prove the actual new combinational expressions equivalent to the original branch case for all 32-bit operand pairs and all eight branch-op encodings. Test equality, signed extremes, opposite signs, adjacent values, and each possible highest-differing two-bit leaf, including the special least-significant seed and sign-conditioned most-significant leaf. Preserve all existing tests and add directed seed cases for all six predicates. Exercise every forwarding-source combination, youngest-writer priority, x0, retained WB operands, load-dependent branches, both prediction errors, target faults, queue-full recovery, blocking M operations and prolonged independent bus stalls. Require identical live retirement, training and recovery cycles and precise RVFI operands, PC, trap and order.

Keep nret=1 and every top-level port, full 32-bit addresses, default-illegal decoding, all memory side effects and handshakes, real and ALTOPS arithmetic, reset/stall priorities and formal bounds. Run unchanged sequential formal including liveness/reg/pc_fwd/unique, both pipeline-test variants, stalled reference cosimulation, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation and all three scored Gowin placement options. No contract or evaluation files change.

title: Bank EX results before selection and flatten their forwarding into execution
motivation:
The champion scores 211.52 iterations/s at 84.388 MHz and 3,989,539
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path starts at MEM/WB data
and crosses EX branch verification into IF. Prior r13s2 removed wide
forwarding ahead of branch comparison, but then forwarding-to-ALU-result
became critical. Structural r13s1 instead shared arithmetic slices with
branch verification and exposed an alu_op-to-recovery path, losing 36.79%.
The promising structural target is the organization of EX result capture
and selection: the current forwarded operands feed many operations whose
results reconverge through a common mux before EX/MEM. Bank those results
at the existing edge and select them as part of the next operand route,
while giving branch verification its own independent comparison lanes.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 211.52 iterations/s at 84.388 MHz and 3,989,539
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path starts at MEM/WB data
and crosses EX branch verification into IF. Prior r13s2 removed wide
forwarding ahead of branch comparison, but then forwarding-to-ALU-result
became critical. Structural r13s1 instead shared arithmetic slices with
branch verification and exposed an alu_op-to-recovery path, losing 36.79%.
The promising structural target is the organization of EX result capture

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the single selected EX/MEM arithmetic-result register with four
parallel result banks and a registered one-hot result class. Integrate bank
selection into the next instruction's operand forwarding, instead of putting
a common ALU-result mux before the capture edge. Pair this organization with
independent branch comparison lanes that select one-bit results after
comparison. This is one structural redesign of the EX feedback network;
retain every instruction stage, execution latency, retirement edge and
predictor policy. Do not pipeline recovery or lengthen division.

Use four 32-bit result banks: arithmetic (ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU), shift
(SLL/SRL/SRA), logic/link (AND/OR/XOR/LUI and PC+4 for JAL/JALR), and M
(the existing multiply/divide completion). Preserve native arithmetic and
the existing real/ALTOPS M units. Compute each bank's result independently;
select only operations within that class before its register. Do not derive
these banks by copying the already-selected common alu.out value. The
logic/link bank alone handles the jump link override, removing the final
jump-versus-full-ALU mux from the other result captures. Preserve a normal
combined ALU output for standalone tests if useful, but do not reconnect
that combined output to the timed EX/MEM bank inputs.

At the existing EX/MEM edge capture all four bank payloads whenever the
older memory stage can advance, including bubbles, independently of late
instruction-valid/execute-wait control. Hold all banks on real dmem stall.
Capture a one-hot class selector alongside the producing instruction;
reset gives a defined selector and payloads. A valid writing instruction
has exactly one class. Use original jump classification to select the link
bank even though the decoded ALU operation is ADD. All pipeline bubbles
still clear valid, reg_write, mem_read, mem_write and the remaining control
metadata. Bank payloads of a bubble may change but can cause no effect.
Retain the dedicated effective_addr register and raw store-data path.

For MEM/WB and RVFI, select the producer's bank result and retain the
champion's load-versus-ALU selection before MEM/WB.wb_data. That short
bank-selection path ends at MEM/WB. For forwarding to EX, expose the four
registered bank words and their class bits directly, not just a selected
32-bit result. For each source derive mutually exclusive route enables
from the existing forwarding selector: original ID/EX value, MEM/WB value,
or one of the four EX/MEM banks. Each bank enable is EX-forward-selected
AND that bank's captured class. Combine masked words with an explicitly
balanced reduction. Preserve EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority and x0 suppression.
Retained MEM/WB forwarding eligibility must not be gated by retirement valid.

Form the actual ALU operands with PC/immediate overrides in these route
enables: AUIPC chooses PC instead of every raw A route, and alu_src chooses
immediate instead of every raw B route. Avoid rebuilding a raw-forwarded
word followed by another PC/immediate mux on the arithmetic path. Keep
separate exact raw rs1/rs2 selection for stores, JALR/effective addresses,
RVFI operands and captured M-operation source values. Do not change operand
values or permit speculative register/memory writes. The intended gain is
removing the common multi-class result selection before EX/MEM and combining
its post-register choice with forwarding rather than serializing two muxes.

Keep branch verification independent of all arithmetic-bank opcode and
carry logic. Use the three architectural forwarding-source candidates on
each side: saved ID operand, selected EX/MEM bank result, and registered
MEM/WB data. Compare the seven nonidentical source pairs in parallel;
EX-versus-EX and WB-versus-WB have constant equality=true, less-than=false.
Each real lane uses the champion's sixteen native two-bit equality/unsigned
ordering leaves and four balanced high/low merge levels. Derive signed
ordering from original sign bits. Select the one-bit equality/ordering
results using the existing forwarding selectors, then apply the captured
branch_eq/branch_signed/branch_unsigned/branch_invert controls. A source
pair must never use a subtract result whose mode depends on alu_op. This
avoids the precise r13s1 failure while moving wide source selection after
comparison, as demonstrated by r13s2. Keep the EX-bank selection confined
to its candidate; the WB and original-source comparison lanes must not
traverse that mux. Preserve original raw RVFI operand values separately.

Keep the original legal/aligned actual_taken, ex_accept including
!execute_wait, architectural pc_next, redirect edge, recovery target,
training edge and target-fault behavior. Keep the 64-entry predictor,
registered training, fall-through queue and all hazards unchanged. Do not
add early load forwarding, a recovery register, speculative arithmetic
requests or different memory acceptance. Preserve the existing two-edge
multiply and nine-edge divide transfer schedules, captured operands and
held completion. Keep nret=1, decoder default-illegal behavior, all memory
and RVFI ports, and every proof/benchmark invariant.

Expect an eight percent fitness gain, with low confidence: the final banked
execution topology has not been implemented or measured. Register banks add
roughly 96 physical payload bits over the single result register before
synthesis, plus class metadata; comparison replication adds LUTs and may
increase routing cost. Keep the implementation comfortably below 10,000
logic cells. A naive bank mux feeding the original forwarding mux defeats
the architectural purpose; inspect the timed netlist paths to establish
that bank and operand routes are combined. General shifter, memory, divider
and branch-recovery paths can still limit the clock, so acceptance depends
on measured median Fmax times measured iterations/cycle.

Local disposable probes during hypothesis generation reinforce the need to
address competing feedback paths; they are not evidence for this unbuilt
banked design. Delaying recovery one cycle reached 85.259 MHz but increased
CoreMark cycles and failed liveness. Registered logical fetch rebasing kept
3,989,539 cycles and passed all 53 unchanged formal checks, but reached only
83.651 MHz. A smaller radix-16 divider reduced area to 4,403 logic cells and
971 registers, yet reached only 83.931 MHz; its longer schedule failed

title: MEM-stage prediction verification with recovery-before-retirement interlock
motivation:
The champion scores 211.52 iterations/s at 84.388 MHz and 3,989,539 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs from registered WB data through EX prediction verification to fetch-queue payload control. Larger direction tables offer limited headroom: the prior retirement-order model recorded only about 51,419 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs. Target the location of prediction verification rather than predictor capacity.

Prior r8s2 moved conditional verification to MEM and failed liveness; r10s2 and r12s1 deferred only load-dependent branches and retained an ordinary EX-to-IF recovery path plus age arbitration. The proposed single redesign verifies every control transfer at MEM, and retains a correcting instruction until the fetch correction has been applied. This preserves a bounded retirement gap while allowing conditional branches to consume a preceding load's registered WB value without an EX load-use bubble.

A disposable probe during this proposal registered EX recovery and held EX/MEM plus WB advancement for its correction cycle. It passed all 53 unchanged fast formal checks, including liveness, and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation. It measured 4,055,160 bracketed cycles and 84.150 MHz for placement option 1, so that probe alone does NOT meet acceptance. This establishes evidence for the recovery interlock, not performance or correctness of the final MEM-verification design. Other local EX-only verification simplifications also failed to show sufficient timing gains.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move prediction verification for all BRANCH, JAL and JALR instructions to the existing MEM stage and introduce one recovery-before-retirement interlock for a mispredicted control transfer. This is one predictor-resolution architecture. Retain the current 64 persistent bimodal counters, registered training-event update, direct-target fetch prediction, four-entry fall-through queue, arithmetic units and instruction latencies. No predictor-size sweep, cache, return stack or arithmetic redesign is proposed.

EX prepares control-transfer packets but does not generate redirects or conditional training. Carry the original predicted_taken, the four predecoded branch predicate bits, and two deferred-load operand flags in EX/MEM. Reuse its PC, instruction, source identities, source values and direct target; retain the existing full forwarded JALR sum with bit zero cleared. Capture an unambiguous resolved jump target, either in the existing jump pc_next payload or a dedicated field. Preserve JAL/JALR link PC+4 and their target-alignment write suppression. Conditional outcome, conditional target fault and final architectural conditional pc_next are determined only in MEM. Remove the now-unused EX conditional comparator from timed logic.

For a conditional branch whose source matches the valid immediately older EX/MEM load's nonzero rd, mark that operand deferred. Do not capture the load's EX/MEM arithmetic/address result as its branch operand. Capture a fallback value selected from a matching retained MEM/WB register writer, otherwise the original ID/EX operand. Other branch operands use ordinary EX forwarding. In MEM, replace a deferred operand with registered MEM/WB.wb_data only when that immediately older producer actually has reg_write set and its nonzero rd matches. Check retained control and identity, not rvfi_valid or the valid-gated regfile write pulse: WB data/control remains a legitimate source through a hold. If the older load trapped and suppressed its register write, use the saved fallback. Apply repair independently to both sources and report the repaired values in branch RVFI.

Suppress the load-use bubble only for a positively decoded legal conditional-branch head with funct3 in {0,1,4,5,6,7}. Its comparison now occurs after the load data has entered WB. Keep every other load-use interlock, including JALR, and retain the existing data-bus backpressure: an unready older memory operation prevents the branch from leaving EX. Do not add a combinational memory-data-to-branch path; repair exclusively from registered WB data.

MEM compares the saved/repaired operands using the champion's balanced native two-bit leaves and captured predicate controls. Compute the actual legal aligned transfer, architectural resolved next PC, target fault and prediction mismatch. A taken misaligned branch traps, suppresses its transfer and resolves architecturally to PC+4; a not-taken branch with a misaligned encoded target remains legal. Direct JAL is checked against its captured prediction; an aligned legal JALR remains an unpredicted transfer. Illegal instructions neither redirect nor train. For direct control, correction is the alternative to the captured prediction, predicted_taken ? PC+4 : saved direct target; JALR uses its saved masked target. Never substitute this alternative address for resolved RVFI pc_next when no correction is needed.

Use MEM as the sole recovery producer. Eliminate EX-vs-MEM redirect arbitration entirely. A valid control packet has no data-memory transaction, so unrelated io_dmemReady must not delay its verification. Correct predictions advance normally to WB and permit the younger EX instruction to advance in the same cycle. Train a legal, non-faulting conditional branch exactly once when it actually advances from MEM to WB, with its real condition and its own PC[7:2]. Route this MEM event through the existing IF training-event register. A correcting branch trains on its final advancement, not on both verification cycles.

Define a one-bit recovery_applied_q, reset to zero. On the first MEM mismatch for the held control packet, assert correction = mismatch && !recovery_applied_q. On that edge: update the IF PC and invalidate the entire fetch queue; flush ID/EX with priority over any younger execution wait; hold the resolving EX/MEM packet; and clear MEM/WB.valid while retaining all of its data/control for forwarding. Set recovery_applied_q. Suppress the younger EX instruction's multiply/divide requests and EX/MEM acceptance on this correction cycle. No wrong-path load or store may enter the memory stage. Because the resolving packet is a control transfer, holding it cannot duplicate a data-bus transaction.

On the following cycle the same EX/MEM control packet remains present, but recovery_applied_q suppresses repeated correction. Advance that packet to WB exactly once, clear recovery_applied_q when it leaves, and allow EX/MEM to take the flushed younger bubble. The corrected instruction can now enter ID/EX. MEM/WB retained the older producer through the correction edge, so any deferred branch source stays stable until this final advancement. Reset cancels the interlock. If any additional internal hold is introduced, retain recovery_applied_q and the packet until the actual advancement; never clear the bit merely because a clock elapsed while holding the same packet.

The correcting instruction therefore remains an actual pipeline resident until after its correction is applied. Its link write, if any, and its sole RVFI retirement occur together at the real WB boundary. This is not an RVFI-only delay or a fabricated retirement. It delays both the correction path and the correcting instruction's retirement relative to EX verification, so the gap from that retirement to a slow instruction on the corrected path need not grow as in the failed r8s2 design. The existing liveness proof must still pass unchanged for the final design; the EX-interlock probe is evidence, not a substitute for that proof.

Maintain the normal MEM load/store implementation and WB payload-retention semantics. Give recovery hold higher priority than a younger EX capture, and recovery squash higher priority than a younger execute_wait. The resolving packet has no memory request, so an apparent data stall from the wrong-path EX instruction cannot block correction. Forwarding metadata must reflect the actual held EX/MEM and retained WB registers on the interlock edge and refresh normally afterward. Preserve youngest-writer priority, x0, complete inert bubble controls, full-width addresses, decoder default-illegal behavior, nret=1 and every top-level IO/RVFI port. Leave multiplier/divider arithmetic, ALTOPS schedules and all external contracts unchanged.

The estimated fitness gain is six percent with low confidence. Load-dependent branches can save the roughly 2.7 percent cycle opportunity seen in earlier experiments, while one extra recovery cycle per miss/JALR consumes part of that saving. The final delayed training schedule and stalls require fresh measurement; no final cycle count is asserted. Removing EX comparison and all EX recovery arbitration may improve both branch timing and loading on the shared EX operand network. Competing general-ALU/divider paths, the new WB-to-MEM comparison path, and added timed operand registers remain material risks. Acceptance requires more than 221.24992 iterations/s using the measured bracketed cycles and median of all scored Gowin placements. No final implementation, median timing result or accepted gain is claimed.

Validate the two-phase interlock first with the unchanged liveness, unique, reg, pc_fwd and pc_bwd checks, followed by the full unchanged fast formal suite. Add directed branch-recovery-then-DIV/REM cases, including JALR recovery followed by blocking arithmetic. Exercise every branch condition, both repaired operands, a trapping preceding load and fallback to a retained WB writer. Place stores, loads, jumps and MUL/DIV immediately behind a misprediction and prove that no younger request, register write, retirement or training survives correction. Check that a pending link instruction writes once at its delayed architectural retirement and that target instructions see its forwarded link correctly.

Adapt only microarchitectural timing observers to MEM verification and the explicit interlock; retain all architectural assertions and formal bounds. Verify one correction, one eventual retirement and one training event per eligible packet, complete queue invalidation even when full or imem unready, correct register holds on both interlock edges, reset cancellation, contiguous RVFI order, repaired RVFI operands and exact resolved PCs/traps. Run stalled reference cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks, then all scored vendor placement options. The prior EX-interlock probe's unchanged pipeline observers expected EX-cycle training/recovery and therefore did not all pass; those observations must be updated to the specified MEM schedule without weakening correctness checks.

title: Shorten ALU shifts with parallel coarse selection and fine shifting
motivation:
The champion scores 211.52 iterations/s at 84.388 MHz and 3,989,539
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent branch-only changes expose a competing
forwarding-to-ALU-result path: r14s0 ends at EX/MEM.alu_result through
u_alu, and achieves only 0.10 percent. Earlier operand-candidate replication
and banked result forwarding regress badly. The three native variable
shifts in the base ALU are a localized opportunity to reduce mux depth and
routing without changing execution latency or the established bypass loop.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 211.52 iterations/s at 84.388 MHz and 3,989,539
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent branch-only changes expose a competing
forwarding-to-ALU-result path: r14s0 ends at EX/MEM.alu_result through
u_alu, and achieves only 0.10 percent. Earlier operand-candidate replication

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the combinational SLL/SRL/SRA implementation with a factored
coarse/fine barrel shifter. Keep left and right data paths separate to
avoid introducing direction-dependent bit reversal before or after the
shifter. Decode b[4:3] into four mutually exclusive coarse enables.
For each direction, form four constant-wired candidates shifted by
0,8,16,24 positions, mask them with the coarse enables, and combine
them with an explicitly balanced OR tree. Then shift this intermediate
by b[2:0] using ordinary conditional shifts by one, two and four bits,
in that order. This replaces serial coarse data selection with a
parallel decode/mask/reduction network and keeps fine shifting local.

Share the right-shift network between SRL and SRA with fill equal to
(op == ALU_SRA) AND a[31]. Use that same fill for every coarse candidate
and all three fine stages; logical right and left shifts fill with zero.
Keep full 32-bit values, use only b[4:0], and handle shamt=0 exactly.
Keep the current ALU result case and operation encodings, forwarded
operands, address/branch adders, comparator, multiplier, divider,
request/completion schedules, predictor and pipeline registers intact.
This is one local data-selection topology change, with no extra stage,
cycle, bypass source, prediction policy or memory behavior.

Preserve every real and ALTOPS M-extension formula and handshake, all
reset/hold/bubble priorities, decoder default-illegal behavior, nret=1
and the complete RVFI and memory interfaces. Prove combinational shift
equivalence for arbitrary operands and every shift amount, including
ignored upper b bits. Retain all tests and extend ALU shift tests for
all 32 amounts, both signs, walking bits and random words; run existing
pipeline tests, unchanged formal and stalled reference cosimulation.
Require the canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks and the
same bracketed cycle count. Compare all scored Gowin placement options.
At unchanged cycles, acceptance needs median Fmax above approximately
88.269 MHz, corresponding to more than 221.24992 iterations/s. The
principal risks are coarse-enable fanout, OR-tree mapping, and another
EX or divider path becoming the limiting path.

A disposable prototype measured Gowin placement options 0/1/2 at
83.019/85.563/85.563 MHz, median 85.563 MHz. The champion reproduced
84.388 MHz in option 1. The prototype uses 5,805 logic cells, 1,256
registers, 49 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Canonical stalled
CoreMark passes the unchanged CRC/UART/bounds/completion/marker validator
in exactly 3,989,539 bracketed cycles. This projects 214.468388 iterations/s,
only 1.39 percent above 211.52 and below the 4.6 percent acceptance margin;
the integer impact estimate rounds to one percent. No accepted improvement
is claimed. Competing branch recovery and divider paths limit the gain.

An exhaustive Yosys SAT miter using the actual replacement shift network
proved equivalence for every 32-bit a and b and every five-bit op, including
all arithmetic-fill and ignored-upper-b cases. Both existing ALU suite
variants and both existing pipeline suite variants pass with unchanged
assertions. Stalled selftest reference cosimulation matches all 115
retirements. Full sequential riscv-formal was not run during this proposal;
the implementation must still pass every unchanged orchestrator gate.

The four-way coarse implementation is the strongest single local change
measured in this session. A 32-way shifter, fully masked fine selection, shared
bit-reversal shifter, balanced ALU comparison and forwarding-retiming
probes were slower and are not part of this proposal. Reversing the fine
stage order, doing all three fine stages before coarse selection, and
pairing this shifter with r14s0's seeded branch comparator also regressed
in placement option 1; retain the specified coarse-first 1/2/4 topology.

title: Retime forwarding into complete operand capture before execution
motivation:
The champion reaches 211.52 iterations/s at 84.388 MHz and 3,989,539
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path starts at MEM/WB data,
traverses EX operand forwarding and branch verification, and ends in the
fetch queue. Recent structural attempts r13s1 and r14s1 lost 36.79% and
27.83% by adding arithmetic-control or bank-selection dependencies to EX
recovery. Moving recovery later also lost fitness. The untried structural
opportunity is to change which side of the ID/EX edge resolves register
dependencies: capture complete, current operands before execution so that
branches and address generation no longer begin with a forwarding mux.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion reaches 211.52 iterations/s at 84.388 MHz and 3,989,539
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path starts at MEM/WB data,
traverses EX operand forwarding and branch verification, and ends in the
fetch queue. Recent structural attempts r13s1 and r14s1 lost 36.79% and
27.83% by adding arithmetic-control or bank-selection dependencies to EX
recovery. Moving recovery later also lost fitness. The untried structural
opportunity is to change which side of the ID/EX edge resolves register
dependencies: capture complete, current operands before execution so that
branches and address generation no longer begin with a forwarding mux.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace EX-stage operand forwarding with decode-side result forwarding
into the existing ID/EX operand registers. This is a retiming of the
execution feedback network, not an additional pipeline stage. An ordinary
ALU producer in EX forwards its combinational, architecturally selected
result to the younger instruction's operand capture on the same edge that
installs the producer in EX/MEM. A producer in MEM supplies its selected
ALU/link or ready, extended load result before MEM/WB capture. WB remains
available through the register file's existing write-first read behavior.
Thus every instruction enters EX with final raw rs1/rs2 values, held for
its entire execution. Remove the old EX/MEM and MEM/WB input muxes and
pre-edge forwarding-match machinery from the execution datapath.

For an incoming valid instruction, prioritize an actually completing,
legal EX writer over a completing legal MEM writer over the write-first
register-file value; suppress x0 and nonwriters. EX forwarding uses the
same final ADD/logic/shift/compare, PC+4, or completed M result that will
enter EX/MEM, with target-fault suppression applied to write eligibility.
Never forward an EX load's effective address as register data. Retain the
existing one-cycle load-use interlock: when the load is in MEM and ready,
capture its fully extended result into the waiting consumer's operands.
MEM eligibility incorporates memory-alignment faults. If a newer producer
of a needed source is unavailable, hold or bubble according to the existing
hazard schedule; never silently fall back to an older value.

Implement source selection beside the ID operand registers. For each
source, x is an enabled nonzero matching EX destination; m is an enabled
nonzero matching MEM destination AND NOT x. Combine (x AND EX value),
(m AND MEM value), and (NOT x AND NOT m AND register-file value) as three
mutually exclusive masked words. Select PC/immediate after that raw
selection when forming A/B. Keep EX eligibility qualified by ex_accept,
post-target-fault reg_write, not-illegal and not-load; keep MEM eligibility
qualified by valid, not-hold_wb, post-alignment reg_write and not-illegal.
The measured prototype uses these qualifications and separate override
muxes. An alternative folding the overrides into wider route masks while
dropping redundant readiness qualifiers reached only 83.076 MHz; avoid
importing that different circuit into this proposal.

Form a shared pair of execution-operand registers at the ID/EX edge:
A selects PC for AUIPC and the complete raw rs1 otherwise; B selects
immediate for alu_src and the complete raw rs2 otherwise. Feed base
arithmetic and branch comparison directly from these same registers.
Branches have neither override, so their A/B values are the exact raw
architectural operands. Feed the dedicated address/JALR adder from A plus
immediate: memory instructions and JALR cannot select the AUIPC override.
This removes PC/immediate selection from the execute arithmetic path and
avoids an additional live raw-rs1 register duplicating A for branches and
addresses. Preserve separate exact raw rs1/rs2 captures for RVFI, including
nominally unused instruction fields, and use raw rs2 for stores, never B
when B holds an immediate. Raw rs1 state used only by RVFI can be pruned
naturally by the timed synthesis. Preserve original M source reporting.
Keep one selected EX/MEM result register; do not introduce result banks,
replicated complete ALUs, a later branch-resolution stage or load-to-EX
combinational forwarding. Use the current independent balanced branch
comparator, existing ALU arithmetic and existing M-extension units.

Separate payload capture from bubble/kill control. When ID/EX is enabled,
operand payloads may capture even when flush or missing instruction
availability makes the instruction a bubble. Reset initializes state;
dmem stalls and execute waits hold a valid instruction and all its complete
operands. Bubble/flush must still clear all side-effect controls and valid.
Do not route EX redirect through the operand-data mux or feed producer
eligibility from the younger instruction's acceptance/flush. Producer data
and eligibility must depend only on that producer's current registered
state, its own arithmetic/trap result and downstream readiness. Avoid a
combinational cycle through hazard, decode acceptance and EX forwarding.

Preserve the four-entry fetch queue, predictor and training, EX recovery
timing, single-cycle base operations, two-edge multiply, nine-edge divide,
memory request acceptance and original load-use bubbles. Capture M operands
only once; retain completed results under backpressure. Completing M
instructions may forward to the younger operand capture on their transfer
edge. Older WB/MEM producers draining during an execution hold must not
change the held instruction's source values. Preserve nret=1, all external
ports, exact RVFI source/result/PC/memory fields, order increments, default
illegal decoding and all existing correctness and liveness checks.

The expected gain is shorter branch/recovery and address paths plus
elimination of serial source and PC/immediate selection before arithmetic.
The main risk is moving the bottleneck to EX-result-to-ID operand capture,
especially DSP completion or the register-file fallback path; a retiming
alone does not guarantee improvement. Require measured median Gowin Fmax
times measured CoreMark iterations/cycle, with the canonical CRCs, UART,
address bounds, marker brackets and randomized bus stalls. The initial
prediction is a 5% fitness gain at unchanged bracketed cycles. At the
champion cycle count, acceptance needs Fmax above about 88.27 MHz and
fitness above 221.24992 iterations/s. Do not weaken formal depth or gates.

Local disposable prototype evidence for this exact shared-operand layout:
canonical stalled CoreMark passed the existing CRC/UART/bounds/marker
validator at 3,989,539 cycles, and stalled selftest reference cosimulation
matched all 115 retirements. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured
84.562/88.538/88.538 MHz, for median 88.538 MHz, 5,895 logic cells,
1,273 registers, 49 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. The resulting
estimated fitness is 221.92539 iterations/s, +4.919% over 211.52.
This narrowly clears the threshold in the probe; it is not an accepted
implementation result, and final RTL must repeat all unchanged gates.
All 53 formal tasks passed using the unchanged single-retire wrapper,
check configuration and depths, including register consistency, liveness,
PC forwarding and unique order. These are ALTOPS proofs; they do not prove

title: MEM prediction verification with recovery isolated from forwarding metadata
motivation:
The champion scores 211.52 iterations/s at 84.388 MHz and 3,989,539 bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md and the predictor experiments establish limited accuracy-only headroom: a prior retirement-order model estimated 51,419 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs. The opportunity is prediction verification and recovery timing.

The r14s2 MEM verifier passed formal and cosimulation and reduced measured cycles to 3,937,748, but scored only 182.44 at 71.840 MHz. Its worst path ran from the resolving branch's saved operand through MEM recovery and EX control to u_fwd/rs1_ex_match_q. Recovery was allowed to control forwarding metadata for a younger consumer that recovery simultaneously destroys. That is a removable dependency, not a necessary part of branch verification. Its MEM operand repair also rechecked the identity and write eligibility of an immediately older load whose relationship can be established before the EX/MEM edge.

Fresh disposable EX-only probes during this proposal did not establish the acceptance margin. Seven parallel comparison lanes on the current parent reached 85.416 MHz on placement option 1 and retained exactly 3,989,539 validated CoreMark cycles. Other predicate/recovery formulations and a smaller three-lane comparison were slower on that placement. The seven-lane probe passed both pipeline-test configurations after updating packed-field observers, but its clock result remains below the roughly 88.27 MHz required at unchanged cycles. Therefore the final proposal instead targets the specific avoidable feedback in MEM verification; it does not combine these comparator experiments with another category.
